title: Sewing 101 (Main)
description: In this 90-minute workshop, you’ll learn the basics of sewing machine operation and safety. This session will cover machine setup, basic functions, threading the machine, reloading the bobbin, sewing straight stitches, and recognizing when stitch tension has gone awry. We’ll also cover some safety best practices when operating a sewing machine. As we learn together, we’ll work on a simple sewing project—a drawstring bag—which most students will be able to complete by the end of the class. You must complete Hive Safety Training before registering for this workshop. If you have not completed the training, you will be removed from the class—even if you plan to take it later. To take Safety Training, come to The Hive during Open Shop to watch a ten-minute video or take a Safety Training class. Check hours on our calendar: [link]. Please arrive on time. If you are more than 10 minutes late, you will not be able to join the class.

title: Linocut Printmaking (Central Square)
description: In this class students will be introduced to the printmaking process of linocut. The class will cover techniques in carving linoleum, composition, ink mixing, and printing. At their own pace students will learn how to create a design and carve it in linoleum using carving tools. Students will learn how to ink and print their linoleum blocks by hand. In a relaxed and welcoming environment students will create many beautiful prints of their own as well as collaborate with their classmates. This class is suitable for beginners and can be adjusted for all levels of experience. This class is taught by Brooke Lambert, a professional printmaker and painter. She holds a BFA from Massachusetts College of Art and Design and shows her work widely in New England, New York, and beyond. Brooke works in Studio 291 at Western Avenue Studios & Lofts in Lowell, MA. She is currently represented by The Society of American Graphic Artists in New York, NY, Galaray House in Boston, MA and Bay View Artisan Gallery in Meredith, NH. Brooke is sponsored by Akua Inks and Speedball Art Products. She has fourteen years of teaching experience and currently teaches adult art workshops and holds artist demos at several locations in New England.

title: Solo Aging Series (Virtual)
description: Join Marni Blank, founder of Begin with the End, for a three-part series designed to give solo agers and those preparing for that possibility the practical tools, emotional support, and community connection they need to plan with confidence. Session 1 (September 17): Building Your Support System Who shows up when life changes? Take an honest look at your current support circle, identify gaps, and understand why the right people in the right roles matters more than we think. Session 2 (October 1): Practical Tools for Planning Ahead This session walks through what documents, decisions and systems to have in place, how to choose the right support and how to organize your financial and digital life so someone can step in if needed. Session 3 (October 15): Taking Action: Mindset, Legacy, and Making it Stick Here we'll address the emotional barriers that keep us stuck, reframing planning as something we do for ourselves and not a sign of decline. This is a virtual presentation, and a link will be provided one hour before each program. Presented in partnership with Cambridge Neighbors.

Everyone—regardless of background or financial situation—can have an estate plan. We will discuss: Financial issues during our lifetimes: power of attorney, homestead declaration, and trusts Health and medical issues: health care proxy, medical directives, and HIPAA authorization Preparing for death: wills and declaration as to remains Estate planning issues specific to veterans and individuals with disabilities will also be discussed.

description: Join the Cambridge Public Library in celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month by welcoming Valeria Luiselli—the acclaimed author of several books, including Tell Me How It Ends and Lost Children Archive, the recipient of the 2021 Dublin Literary Award—for a reading from her new novel, Beginning Middle End. In Beginning Middle End, which received starred reviews from Publisher's Weekly, Kirkus Reviews, and Booklist, Luiselli returns to the road novel form which she innovated in Lost Children Archive. Called "a beautiful, maybe perfect, novel," Beginning Middle End follows a mother and daughter on a quest to start over and find for themselves a new story, in the process weaving "together four generations of women through archaeology, mythology, and the natural world" (W Magazine). After reading from her work, Luiselli will sit in conversation with Eloisa Amezcua, an award-winning poet, translator, and author of Fighting Is Like a Wife. title: YouCan Kits
description: In honor of Save a Life Day and Recovery Month, please join us on Thursday, September 24th from 6-8pm to volunteer to put together overdose prevention kits at the Cambridge Public Library, Main Branch. The You Can initiative (youcan.info) addresses overdose deaths by increasing access to lifesaving skills and resources statewide. Volunteers play a crucial role in this program by assembling the kits that are then mailed out across the state, getting lifesaving resources out to people and families who need them, free of cost. Each kit contains naloxone, fentanyl test strips, and other vital resources. Recovery Month, observed each September, affirms that recovery from substance use and mental health challenges is possible, and shows the city's support for every Cambridge community member in all stages of their recovery journeys. Save a Life Day is a nationwide day of action that promotes year-round widespread naloxone access as one solution to the overdose crisis. Volunteers will be able to leave with a completed kit, if desired. Representatives from the Cambridge Health Department will also be onsite to provide additional resources and support. This program is a partnership between the Massachusetts Department of Public Health and Health Resources in Action (HRiA) and hosted by the Cambridge Public Health Department and Cambridge Public Library.

title: CPL International Briefing: The Situation in Sudan (Main)
description: Sudan has been embroiled in a civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Once allies in Sudan’s transitional government, tensions over the country’s political future and plans to integrate the RSF into the regular military led to open fighting in 2023. More than three years later, the war continues with devastating consequences for civilians, including widespread death, displacement, and food insecurity, creating a severe humanitarian crisis. Join Professor Mai Hassan, Associate Professor of Political Science at MIT and Faculty Director of the MIT-Africa Program, for a conversation about the origins and ongoing consequences of the war, its humanitarian impact, and the challenges facing Sudan’s future. Registration is required.

Join us for Poly Talk, an intimate discussion dedicated to the complexities of polyamory and consensual non-monogamy (CNM) through the queer lens. This is a space to dismantle hetero-mononormative stigmas and celebrate the diverse ways our community shows up for and with one another. Pull up a chair. Join our affair. title: Solo Aging Series (Virtual)
description: Join Marni Blank, founder of Begin with the End, for a three-part series designed to give solo agers and those preparing for that possibility the practical tools, emotional support, and community connection they need to plan with confidence. Session 1 (September 17): Building Your Support System Who shows up when life changes? Take an honest look at your current support circle, identify gaps, and understand why the right people in the right roles matters more than we think. Session 2 (October 1): Practical Tools for Planning Ahead This session walks through what documents, decisions and systems to have in place, how to choose the right support and how to organize your financial and digital life so someone can step in if needed. Session 3 (October 15): Taking Action: Mindset, Legacy, and Making it Stick Here we'll address the emotional barriers that keep us stuck, reframing planning as something we do for ourselves and not a sign of decline. This is a virtual presentation and a link will be provided one hour before each program. Presented in partnership with Cambridge Neighbors.

title: Solo Aging Series (Virtual)
description: Join Marni Blank, founder of Begin with the End, for a three-part series designed to give solo agers and those preparing for that possibility the practical tools, emotional support, and community connection they need to plan with confidence. Session 1 (September 17): Building Your Support System Who shows up when life changes? Take an honest look at your current support circle, identify gaps, and understand why the right people in the right roles matters more than we think. Session 2 (October 1): Practical Tools for Planning Ahead This session walks through what documents, decisions and systems to have in place, how to choose the right support and how to organize your financial and digital life so someone can step in if needed. Session 3 (October 15): Taking Action: Mindset, Legacy, and Making it Stick Here we'll address the emotional barriers that keep us stuck, reframing planning as something we do for ourselves and not a sign of decline. This is a virtual presentation and a link will be provided one hour before each program. Presented in partnership with Cambridge Neighbors.

title: CPL Presents America Unfinished: 250 Years of Law and Governance (Main)
description: Join editors Alexandra Natapoff and Guy-Uriel Charles, along with contributors to America Unfinished: 250 Years of Law and Governance, for a discussion of this new collection of essays marking America’s 250th anniversary. America Unfinished brings together more than 50 legal scholars from the Harvard Law School faculty to examine a pivotal moment in American law and governance. The collection’s 62 essays explore topics including the expansion of executive power, the relationship between workers, consumers, and markets, democratic accountability in a market-driven economy, and the future of knowledge and governance institutions amid rapid technological change. Contributors include Stephen Breyer, Tomiko Brown-Nagin, Noah Feldman, Annette Gordon-Reed, Randall Kennedy, Jill Lepore, Lawrence Lessig, Bruce H. Mann, Martha Minow, and Cass R. Sunstein. Sponsored by the Cambridge Public Library and the Cambridge Public Library Foundation.

title: Nelward
description: Nelward nelward is an innovative music artist creating funky electronic artpop for the internet age. Early on, the melodies of classic Nintendo games were etched into his ADHD brain and never seemed to leave. Drawing from a wide array of influences, nelward enjoys the explorative aspect of music creation and is not one to dwell in one sound for too long. He is also known for the colorful and whimsical art direction in his often self-produced videos. In 2017, his first EP Alive in Screen established his foundational sound. The subsequent success of the new jack swing/nu metal banger Ghost / Getting Better and bubblegum pop earworm Never Wanna Fall in Love With U established him as a force to be reckoned with in the independent electronic music scene. 2020’s Eat Your Dreams EP delved into heavier subject matter while tightening nelward’s knack for catchy songwriting. 2024’s single THE RUNAROUND combines infectious earworms while embracing musical exploration. Nelward is known for his animated live performances, completing a 40+ date tour of North America and Europe with TWRP from 2024-2025. In 2025 the nelward live band was born, representing a distinct chapter in the evolution of his live performance. Nelward represents a growing segment of independent electronic artists who are building significant followings through digital platforms while creating innovative multimedia art experiences. Justice Cow is the cosmic gumbo of Jessica Kion. She grew up in a musical family which meant pressing rewind until she had transcribed every word of the “Grease” soundtrack and being forced to sing barbershop quartet family-style in the car. For over a decade she has toured extensively across the US and abroad, equally at home in living rooms, rock clubs, and festival stages. description: Build a wooden model of an iconic Nintendo character! Each participant will be given a set of painted wooden blocks that correspond with their chosen character. Producing music with his best friend in a bedroom, the music is genre fluid, with cinematic elements, and built around mood and storytelling. He has built a whole universe to play in and explore. title: Onelouddrawing
description: ONELOUDDRAWING Jonah / onelinedrawing with a full band doing Far’s Tin Cans on its 30th anniversary, plust stuff from New End’s Thriller & the new onelinedrawing album RAINBOWMACHINE ARTIST BIO: onelinedrawing is Jonah Matranga of Far, Gratitude, New End Original, and more. On September 18, Iodine Recordings will release RAINBOWMACHINE, the new album from onelinedrawing. The album was produced by Jay Maas. It’s the loudest, wildest onelinedrawing record yet. The tracks above are from the album. There will also be the first full-band onelinedrawing shows in forever in September and October, celebrating the 30th anniversary of Far’s TIn Cans With Strings To You, the 25th anniversary of Thriller, and of course the new album. Jonah started onelinedrawing in 1998, just as his first band, post-hardcore / emo misfits Far, was breaking up. The first onelinedrawing releases were a cassette on POPROCKIT, a label started by Kevin Seconds (7 Seconds). Then came the Sketchy EPs, first self-released, then in various forms on various indie labels (Crank, Revelation, Corrupted Image). During that time, onelinedrawing pioneered sliding-scale pricing for downloads and merch, monthly crowdfunded patronage (eventually released as the Always New albums), and Unique Recordings. During that time, onelinedrawing toured with and/or released music with Rival Schools, The Juliana Theory, Coheed & Cambria, Dashboard Confessional, Murder By Death, The Weakerthans, Jimmy Eat World, and more. onelinedrawing’s most recent studio album is Tenderwild, on Iodine Records. Iodine also recently released Sketchbook, a collection of early onelinedrawing recordings 1999-2001. onelinedrawing also has two albums (VISITOR and THE VOLUNTEERS) still on Jade Tree / Epitaph. Over 30 years, several projects, dozens of albums, hundreds of songs, and thousands of shows, Jonah Matranga has influenced countless artists: Deftones, Frank Turner, Thursday, My Chemical Romance, Walter Schreifels, and Chris Carraba. title: Hunter Flynn: Back to My Roots Tour
description: Hunter Flynn: Back to My Roots Tour Presented by The Rockwell and Peachtree Entertainment. Hunter Flynn is a Kentucky-born singer-songwriter and visual artist whose work resonates with emotional honesty and a deep connection to Appalachian culture. Raised in Pulaski County, Flynn’s path to music and art wasn’t a straight line—it was forged through adversity and personal transformation. In early 2022, after surviving a life-altering car accident, he decided to fully embrace his creative passions, launching a music career rooted in authenticity, vulnerability, and soul. Drawing inspiration from the landscapes and stories of Appalachia, Flynn blends elements of folk, country, soul, and gospel into a genre-defying sound he calls Appalachian Soul Music. His lyrics, often reflective and raw, tell stories of pain, redemption, resilience, and identity—underscored by his powerful vocals and minimalist arrangements. These qualities are showcased in his debut EP, Appalachian Soul, released in May 2023, which quickly gained traction for its emotional depth and stripped-back sincerity. Learn more about Hunter Flynn and his music at www.hunterflynn.com . ARTIST BIOS: Julia Minken: Best known for co-writing viral hit songs with French electropop sensation Kid Francescoli, Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin steps into her own with her debut album Not Ready, co-created and produced with her husband Andrew Sudhibhasilp. Blending warm, folk-tinged vocals with nostalgic dance-floor energy and introspection, Minkin “finds her own creative voice, shimmering, rhythmic, and heartfelt—both bold and refreshingly sincere” (Thoughts Words Actions). Bowling Shoes: Melding innovative art-pop experimentalism with indie-rock nuance and arena-ready hooks, Boston, MA’s Bowling Shoes craft eminently catchy music sprinkled with delightful touches of subversive noise Cate Yoder: A double and electric bassist and guitarist from Richmond, Virginia, Cate Yoder learns about her environment through exploring, inventing, and performing a multitude of genres or really any music she can get hands on. Since being established primarily as a bass player, she is diving into the songwriting indie folk role with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. With airy melodies, detailed guitar, piano, and percussive elements, and bitter lyrics, she hopes to share her experience of finding solace and comfort in a complex world. title: GHOSTWOMAN
description: GHOSTWOMAN GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. The music has always been beautifully inhospitable, earned only by those curious enough to seek it out. — Dine Alone Records Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: Show age differs by the day. title: The Sloppy Boys
description: The Sloppy Boys The Sloppy Boys are a Los Feliz, California based party rock band comprised of Mike Hanford, Jefferson Dutton, and Tim Kalpakis from the comedy group The Birthday Boys . title: ☀️ Summer Series: The Summer Throwdown
description: The Summer Series concludes with The Summer Throwdown, MC’ed by the legendary Megatron, a high-energy end-of-season celebration featuring DJs, live performances, and an electrifying dance battle. This event brings the community together one final time to close out the summer with music and movement.

title: Lift Every Voice: BIPOC Play Festival
description: A signature MAC program, Lift Every Voice amplifies the work of BIPOC playwrights, poets, and spoken word artists through staged readings and performances. The festival creates space for artists to share new work while fostering meaningful dialogue between creators and audiences.

title: The Fabric of Us: A Celebration of Black Fashion Through the Decades
description: This annual showcase celebrates the evolution of Black style, identity, and cultural expression across generations. Through original designs inspired by movements ranging from the Harlem Renaissance to contemporary fashion culture, the event highlights the lasting influence of Black creativity and innovation.

title: MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival
description: A new addition to MAC’s programming, MAC Movement Makers: The M³ Festival is a multi-day celebration of contemporary dance and movement-based performance. Bringing together choreographers, performers, and audiences, the festival creates opportunities for artistic experimentation, collaboration, and dialogue while expanding MAC’s presence within the dance community.Across the season, MAC continues to deepen its investment in artist development, signature cultural programming, and community-centered experiences that position the organization as both a creative incubator and a gathering place for diverse communities.Each performance will include the works of two dance companies, followed by a Q+A with one company.Tickets to individual performances are $40Choose tickets to any two performances, and receive 25% off your order!Choose tickets to all four performances, and receive 50% off your order!

title: Día de los Muertos Celebration
description: Honoring the rich Mexican tradition of Día de los Muertos, this immersive community celebration features music, dance, storytelling, and altar installations that invite audiences to reflect on ancestry, remembrance, and the enduring bonds between generations.

title: Barbed Wire
description: Each year we celebrate MLK – the person and the weekend – with a performance focused on the legacy of Black America from Civil Rights to today. This year we bring to the stage Barbed Wire, a new work presented in full for the first time on our stage.

title: Oktoberfest at Broadway
description: Let the Bavarian Festivities begin! Celebrate the biggest beer holiday of the year with us at our 2025 Oktoberfest Celebrations. We are serving up double the fun, with two weekends full of prost-ing across both locations. We'll close out the season with a bang at the Broadway Taproom on September 25th & 26th No tickets or reservations are required, but we ask that you RSVP so we can get an idea of numbers (it does not guarantee entry). For General Admission, a $10 fee charged at the door gets you entry and includes a custom 12 oz glass German stein. You drink out of it all day in the taproom, and then it's yours to take home with you! Here's what you can expect this year: 🇩🇪 Craft Beer Galore: An incredible draft list featuring our craft takes on traditional German beers plus some of our favorite seasonal styles: think Lagers, Kolsches, Sours, and beyond. Sip on a classic or discover a new favorite. 🥨 Delicious Eats: Our Italian-inspired permanent pop-up, Controne, is taking a trip to Germany. Feast on giant pretzels, bratwurst, and other mouthwatering German-inspired dishes. 🍺Limited Edition Glass Stein: All attendees will go home with a collectible glass stein to commemorate the occasion. You'll drink out of it all fest, and afterwards it's yours to keep. 🎉 Stein Holding Competitions: Put your strength to the test at our Stein Holding Competitions held throughout both days. Prizes and bragging rights await the winners! 🤩 And don’t forget to wear your finest lederhosen and dirndls - free beers are awarded throughout the event by our festmeister for the best dressed. Get ready to soak in the lively Oktoberfest spirit. Our brewery will be transformed into a festive wonderland, complete with decor, music, games, and expanded drinking zones. Bring your friends, family, and beer-loving pals to raise a toast to this cherished Bavarian tradition. This event is 21+ and all guests must show a valid government-issued photo ID upon entry. title: Cambridge Public Library Book Club
description: Every other month, we team up with the Cambridge Public Library to highlight contemporary works from marginalized voices. All over a fresh, craft beer, of course! We’ll gather in person in our Broadway location’s back taproom on Wednesday, July 1st, at 7:00 pm for our monthly discussion. Grab a beer, cold brew, or kombucha at the front bar, then come find us in the back. The discussion is casual, and all are welcome – even if you don’t finish the book, we’d still love to have you. Copies of the book are available at the Main Library in Cambridge, at 449 Broadway. The e-book and digital audiobook can be borrowed through the Libby app. Let us know if you need help accessing the book. Please note that our taprooms are 21+ and all guests should be prepared to show a valid, current government-issued photo ID at the door. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Brewery Yoga
description: Buy your tickets on Eventbrite! Looking for some healthy weekend plans? Join us for a Sunday morning brewery yoga class at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s Cambridge Crossing (CX) taproom. We’ll gather in the light-filled upstairs taproom for a gentle flow. Space is limited, and reservations are required. Save your spot through Eventbrite here! All yoga levels are welcome! This class is great for beginners, as well as for experienced yogis. We’ll lead you through a guided flow with a focus on stretching, breathing, and light activity – you might work up a light sweat, but nothing too strenuous. Please plan on bringing your own yoga mat. If you don’t have a mat, a large beach towel works as well. The class takes place in our upstairs taproom at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s CX location (110 N First St, Cambridge MA). Your ticket includes full access to the yoga class as well as a beer, cold brew coffee, or kombucha. Parking: There is street parking available, or the parking garage is available for $10 with Lamplighter validation. Show your ticket to a bartender before or after class to validate! This event is 21+ and all guests must show a valid government-issued ID. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com.

title: Broadway Trivia
description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! The game will start at 7:30 pm, and is about two hours long (with plenty of beer breaks, of course). Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Brewery Tour & Tasting
description: Break out your notebook and freshly sharpened No. 2 pencils because we’re going back to school! We're offering brewery tours at our original 284 Broadway location on the first Saturday of every month. Space is limited, so snag your spot right here by purchasing a ticket. Our knowledgeable team will lead you on an interactive, behind-the-scenes tour of the production floor at Lamp, where you’ll learn the essentials of craft beer-making, and how it all works at our compact, Cambridge-based facility. You'll also taste your way through the brewing process, sampling three of our current favorite draft pour picks, plus a special bonus beer to start the sipping syllabus. Will you graduate top of your class? Either way, we think you’ll find your new favorite subject. Each ticket includes: 🍻One 6 oz welcome beer, plus 3 - 5 oz flight glass-sized samples 🚶🏼A 60 min guided tasting and behind-the-scenes brewery tour 📝 Beer School "quiz" and informational answer key 📚 A Lamplighter Beer School diploma :) Questions? Get in touch! events@lamplighterbrewing.com. Please note that this event is 21+ and all guests will be asked to show a valid government-issued ID. Refund Policy We understand that plans sometimes change. If you provide us with more than 24 hours' notice prior to the event start time, we will issue a full refund to your original payment method. Within 24 hours of the start time, we will offer a refund in the form of credit to be used for a future ticketed event hosted by Lamplighter, valid for 1 year. Please note that Eventbrite fees, including processing and service fees, are nonrefundable as they are charged by Eventbrite and not under the control of Lamplighter. Please request refunds through Eventbrite, on your order confirmation page.

title: TCS presents: Shane Torres
description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.Shane Torres is a standup comedian, writer, podcaster, and actor who resides in Brooklyn. Produced by Bert and LeeAnn Kreischer, Shane’s very first special THE BLUE EYED MEXICAN was released in December 2023. Vulture named it as one of the stand-up specials not-to-be-missed in 2023, raving “The Blue Eyed Mexican, stands out for its beautiful directness and keen sense of good storytelling. It’s a refreshing combination of delicate and obscene.” It is available to stream on YouTube. description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.Born and raised in The Bronx, New York, Mark Viera became fascinated with comedy very early on. He became so engaged in the performances of his favorite comic personalities, it didn’t take long before he began to emulate the characters he came to love. Mark’s numerous television credits include performances on the critically acclaimed “Martin Lawrence Presents 1st Amendment Stand-Up”, “Comedy Central’s Russell Simmons Presents Stand-Up at the El Rey”, AXS TV’s “Gotham Comedy Live” a live stand up performance, BET’s “ComicView”, and Comedy Centrals “Gabriel Iglesias Presents: Stand Up Revolution”. Mark’s most recent television appearances are several episodes of Byron Allen’s “Comic Unleashed.” He was recently asked to join comic icon Gabriel Iglesias’s “Unity Through Laughter” world tour. title: TCS presents: Bobcat Goldthwait
description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating. Comedian Bobcat Goldthwait first appeared on the David Letterman Show at the age of 20 and has an ongoing career as a writer, director, actor, voice actor, and stand-up. As a comedian, Bobcat has starred in numerous HBO/Showtime specials, performed in venues worldwide, and even went on tour as an opening act for the band Nirvana. Well-known for his roles in “Scrooged” with Bill Murray and as Zed in the “Police Academy” franchise, Goldthwait has become a well-respected Award- Winning Director, too. His directorial works include feature films World’s Greatest Dad, starring Robin Williams, Willow Creek, starring Bigfoot, God Bless America, Windy City Heat, Sleeping Dogs Lie, and the documentaries Call Me Lucky and Joy Ride. In addition to being a 4x Sundance Alumni, Goldthwait’s films have played internationally, including the Deauville Film Festival and San Sebastian Film Festival. Bobcat has been honored with the German Independent Honorary Award at the Oldenburg Film Festival for his collective works and was awarded “Filmmaker on the Edge” at the Provincetown Film Festival by his hero John Waters. His TV direction includes his series, Misfits and Monsters, Jimmy Kimmel Live, Community, Maron, Those Who Can’t, and many more. Goldthwait has directed numerous standup comedy specials for folks like Patton Oswalt, Marc Maron, Ron Funches, Kyle Kinane, Cameron Esposito, Mo Willems, Gary Gulman, Hari Kondabolu, Eugene Mirman, and Pete Davidson to name a few. Bobcat is currently working on several new film projects and has started his autobiography. The Bar Our Bar opens 1 hour before early shows and 20 minutes before late shows. So come early and grab a drink with us! The Bar also stays open until 1 AM, so stop by after our last show of the evening! **No outside food or beverages allowed**

title: Spotlight Tour: Contained, with Priya Allen ’27
description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk; space is limited. Fee: This is a free event. Accessibility accommodations: If you would like to request accommodations for your visit, please contact Visitor Services at am_register@harvard.edu or 617-495-9400. For more details about accommodations at the museums, please see the Accessibility page. General info: The museum visit page has general guidelines for your visit. On this tour, Priya Allen ’27 will explore the design and politics of historical drinking vessels and containers. The stops on the tour are a Persian jug from the 9th–10th century; a British abolition jug (c. 1810–20); and a samovar designed by Marianne Brandt in the Bauhaus metal workshop in Germany in 1925. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: Free U.S. Citizenship Class Online
description: Prepare for the U.S. citizenship exam with American art in our collections! This fall, the Harvard Art Museums will collaborate with the St. Mark Community Education Program on a free 11-week online course in which you can learn the 128 civics questions and improve your English with interactive lessons featuring American art. St. Mark’s experienced and trained teachers will lead English and civics lessons online every week. On selected weeks, Harvard students in the museums’ Ho Family Student Guide Program will deepen and reinforce these lessons by leading interactive tours of American artworks in our collections. You will have a choice of one of two tracks: Tuesdays (6:30–8:30pm), September 8–November 17, 2026 Wednesdays (6:30–8:30pm), September 9– November 18, 2026 To be eligible for this course, you must have had your green card for 4 years and 9 months, or 2 years and 9 months if your spouse is a U.S. citizen, and be able to speak some English. Instruction is fully in English. Additionally, we ask that you please attend at least 80 percent of the classes. If you register and do not attend class, you are taking a seat from someone else. Please visit St. Mark’s registration page to register by September 1. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums trains students to develop original, research-based tours of the collections. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: Decompress with Rocky Mountains, “Lander’s Peak”
description: Explore Albert Bierstadt’s Rocky Mountains, “Lander’s Peak” through a guided creative writing exercise that invites you to look closely and respond in your own words. No prior writing experience needed. This talk is part of Decompress, a series that allows visitors to linger in quiet contemplation or receive a mindful perspective about artworks in our collections. Whether through a meditative moment, a guided activity, or a reflection with art, the museums are your place to decompress and slow down. Led by: Jeanne Burke, Academic and Public Programs Coordinator, Division of Academic and Public Programs

title: Museum Class: Seeing Art with Matisse
description: This event is at capacity. Explore art history through the perspective of Henri Matisse in this four-week class that takes place in the galleries. With an emphasis on close looking and conversation, Matisse scholar Camran Mani will bring you inside the story of how art history delighted, inspired, and challenged this modern artist, and what he thought about topics from ancient sculpture and Islamic art to Cézanne and beyond. The museum was a space of creative adventure for Matisse—this class aims to make it something similar for you. The class will be held every Thursday from September 10 to October 1.

title: Art Study Center Seminar: Conversations on Conservation
description: In this seminar, you will get a behind-the-scenes view of recent and ongoing projects undertaken in the Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies. Staff members from the Straus Center will share some works in progress and details about the numerous techniques and materials available to them in the care of objects and advancement of technical studies. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections.

title: Second Saturdays Story Time
description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk in the Calderwood Courtyard. Fee: This is a free event. Age restrictions: Ages 3 to 7. Join us for Second Saturdays Story Time in the galleries, an event in partnership with librarians from Cambridge, Somerville, Watertown, and Medford. In this wonderful, art-filled experience held every second Saturday of the month, librarians will choose thematic books to share with you and yours. This program is organized in partnership with the Cambridge Public Library, Somerville Public Library, Watertown Public Library, and Medford Public Library.

title: Gray Area: Truth and Myth in American History
description: Join us on National Voter Registration Day to discuss truth and myth in recent history. Using photographs and paintings from the Social Realism gallery (1320), Tayana Fincher will talk about some of the defining characteristics of American life and what unifies us. This talk is part of Gray Area, a series that features members of our staff exploring artworks that capture the complexities of humanity, political landscapes, ethics, ideologies, power dynamics, and critical thinking in our times. title: Exhibition Preview Day for Friends, Fellows, and Partners
description: We invite Friends, Fellows, and Partners of the museums to be among the first to explore the fascinating exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors (September 18, 2026–January 17, 2027). Discover how an intimate relationship with nature shaped the artistic vision of 19th-century European artists. On Location: Drawing the Outdoors features approximately 140 sketches, watercolors, and pastels by artists including J. M. W. Turner, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, all inspired by the natural world. Organized as a series of thematic journeys through the landscape, the exhibition explores changing ideas about nature, environmental awareness, and artistic identity. It invites visitors to reflect on why these artists’ experiences of the outdoors continue to resonate today. This special preview is our way of thanking you for your support and dedication to the Harvard Art Museums. To become a Friend, Fellow, or Partner, please visit our Support page. Join today to take advantage of this exclusive opportunity. Funding for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. title: Exhibition Opening Program for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors
description: Join us for a special evening celebrating the opening of On Location: Drawing the Outdoors, in which you’ll journey to the 19th century, when European artists stepped outside the studio, explored locations on their walks and travels, and captured their experience in drawings and watercolors. What do their images tell us about working “on location”? Exhibition curators will discuss the techniques, logistical challenges, personal ambitions, and audience expectations that shaped landscape art of the time. Following the program, guests are invited to visit the exhibition on Level 3. This program will be livestreamed. To tune in, check back here soon. On Location features drawings by J. M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. title: Gallery Talk: On Location: Drawing the Outdoors
description: Join former curatorial fellow Susanne Bartels for a gallery talk exploring the special exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors. The talk will examine how 19th-century artists—such as Jean-François Millet, Vincent van Gogh, and Édouard Manet—responded to the far-reaching transformations of industrialization and urbanization reshaping both the land and those who inhabited it. Works on paper, including drawings and watercolors, reveal how artists captured an era in which the landscape was at once a site of hard physical toil and a destination for fashionable escape. title: Materials Lab Workshop: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices
description: Join curatorial assistant for special exhibitions and publications Meghan Grady and Harvard physics professor Aravinthan Samuel for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll first experiment with physical drawing aids, such as perspective frames and camera lucidas, which have helped artists translate complex spaces and details into two dimensions for centuries. Through making, close looking, and a focused gallery visit, participants will explore how such tools work. Grady will share how scientific imaging can inform our understanding of artistic process, accuracy, and style. She researched these techniques for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors, an exhibition featuring 19th-century European drawings and watercolors, and will offer a focused tour explaining how such tools were used in the works on view. Harvard physics professor Aravinthan Samuel will provide an overview of the history of optics in art. During our time together, you’ll create your own gridded frame and take part in a plein air landscape drawing session. You’ll also get the chance to try your hand at applying the devices explored in the workshop. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship Funding for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. title: Gallery Talk: Crafting Perfect Portraits with Photographic Proof Prints
description: Join Madison Brown, co-curator of The Way We Never Were: The American Professional Photographers Collection (August 29, 2026–May 9, 2027), for a discussion about the role of proof prints in the craft of producing polished studio portraits. Rather than capturing a single decisive moment behind the camera, the finished portrait is a result of a multi-step process. The proof prints are used by professional photographers to chart plans for retouching portraits, and photographers’ handwritten notations invite us to explore the extensive and collaborative work behind the sleek finished products. title: Film Screening and Conversation: The Atomic Cafe
description: This film screening and discussion will explore how 1950s American media managed public fear and promoted ideological conformity during the atomic age. The program begins with a screening of The Atomic Cafe, a 1982 documentary compiled entirely from archival footage that demonstrates how U.S. government propaganda, newsreels, military training films, and television broadcasts manufactured a sense of security around the realities of atomic warfare rather than offering genuine reassurance. Duck and Cover (1951), a short educational film produced by the Civil Defense Department, will also be shown. This second film features the animated character Bert the Turtle teaching schoolchildren the supposed ease of surviving an atomic attack through cheerful songs and simple instructions to “duck and cover.” Following the screening, there will be a conversation between The Atomic Cafe directors Jayne Loader and Pierce Rafferty. This program is offered in conjunction with the exhibition The Way We Never Were: The American Professional Photographers Collection. Viewers may find the content of these films disturbing. About the films: The Atomic Cafe, 1982 (The Archives Project, Inc.; English, 88 min.) Duck and Cover, 1951 (Archer Productions; English, 9 min.) Speakers: Jayne Loader, Director Pierce Rafferty, Director Madison Brown (moderator), Smithsonian Institution Postdoctoral Fellow, National Museum of American History, and former John R. and Barbara Robinson Family Curatorial Fellow in Photography, Division of Modern and Contemporary Art, Harvard Art Museums The screening and conversation will take place in Menschel Hall, Lower Level. Doors to the hall will open for seating at 1pm. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the John R. and Barbara Robinson Family Fund for Photography and the M. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. title: Materials Lab Workshop: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint
description: Join paintings conservator Kate Smith and research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll first experiment with a range of pigments from across the ages. You’ll also make your own paints, then compare how the same pigment behaves across different media and surfaces. Learn about the challenges and rewards of re-creating historical paint recipes and the chemical processes behind “lake pigments” like carmine. Then, looking closely at a selection of artworks in the collections, you’ll discover how scientific imaging helps identify materials the artist used; how aging processes shape the appearance of paintings over time; and how museums respond to these changes. You’ll leave with your own test charts, a set of observations about color’s many transformations, and ideas for at‑home experiments. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship

title: A Stroll through History at the Harvard Art Museums
description: This event is at capacity. Starting at Adolphus Busch Hall at 29 Kirkland Street, this tour will explore each location’s significance to Harvard Art Museums’ history through stories drawn from the rich visual and documentary holdings of the museums’ archives. title: Pınar Öğrenci: Good Luck in Germany
description: The 2026 Busch-Reisinger Museum Lecture Berlin-based artist and filmmaker Pınar Öğrenci will discuss her 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany), which is featured in her first major exhibition in the United States, here at the Harvard Art Museums. The film examines the construction of postwar German identity in the Ruhrgebiet, a heavily industrialized region known for coal mining and steel production, as shaped by layered experiences of survival, resistance, and resilience. In it, Öğrenci applies a feminist lens, broadening the history of industrial labor beyond the male worker and the factory. The lecture brings Glück auf in Deutschland into conversation with Öğrenci’s other films, exploring filmmaking as a political practice through which the history of “guest workers” can be connected to ongoing struggles around labor, migration, and belonging. The exhibition Pınar Öğrenci: Glück auf in Deutschland (April 16, 2026–October 18, 2026) includes the 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany) as well as five related collages that reimagine the bodies of workers and their families within the Ruhr landscape and its architecture. Öğrenci’s use of the phrase Glück auf—a common way that miners wish one another a safe return after their physically grueling and dangerous work underground—resonates with the experiences of immigrant communities in present-day Germany facing right-wing extremism. Following the program, guests are invited to visit the exhibition on Level 1. This lecture will be recorded and made available for online viewing; check back shortly after the event for the link to view. This event is part of In Conversation, a series of evening programs that feature local and international curators, artists, scholars, and more. description: We invite Friends, Fellows, and Partners of the museums to explore two fascinating exhibitions at their own pace through a self-guided visit: On Location: Drawing the Outdoors (September 18, 2026–January 17, 2027) and The Way We Never Were: The American Professional Photographers Collection (August 29, 2026–May 9, 2027). In the exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors, discover how an intimate relationship with nature shaped the artistic vision of 19th-century European artists. Featuring approximately 140 sketches, watercolors, and pastels by artists including J. M. W. Turner, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, the exhibition is organized as a series of thematic journeys through the landscape and explores changing ideas about nature, environmental awareness, and artistic identity. It invites visitors to reflect on why these artists’ experiences of the outdoors continue to resonate today. The Way We Never Were explores how professional photography helped shape Americans’ understanding of life after World War II. Drawn from the Harvard Art Museums’ American Professional Photographers Collection, the exhibition features commissioned photographs of weddings, schools, businesses, and other everyday moments that presented an idealized vision of postwar America. These images not only documented the era but also influenced cultural memory by highlighting certain experiences while leaving others out. Through themes of prosperity, suburbia, conformity, and the struggle for equal rights, the exhibition encourages visitors to reconsider the story these photographs tell about the American past. This special preview is our way of thanking you for your support and dedication to the Harvard Art Museums. To become a Friend, Fellow, or Partner, please visit our Support page. Join today to take advantage of this exclusive opportunity. Funding for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fun

title: Artist Talk: Enzo Camacho and Ami Lien
description: The 2026 Nancy Stephenson Nichols Memorial Lecture Join visual artists and Harvard alumni Enzo Camacho (A.B. ’07) and Ami Lien (A.B. ’09) as they share insights and developments into their practice as artistic collaborators. Working between New York, Berlin, and Manila, Camacho and Lien develop research-based, site-specific, and documentary projects to examine histories of labor, land, and resistance in the Philippines. Their research on the enduring influence of Alfonso Ossorio’s mural commission at the Chapel of St. Joseph the Worker on Negros Island has led them to investigate the sugar plantation landscape that grounds this historic site-specific artwork. In their ongoing engagement with Negros Island, the artists focus on the defiant forms of culture-making that emerge out of and in opposition to plantation violence. This program is offered in conjunction with Alfonso Ossorio: Line and Lineage (October 23, 2026–April 11, 2027) in Gallery 1120 at the Harvard Art Museums and Knowledge Is Myth: Chimeric Continuities (October 1–December 13, 2026) at the Carpenter Center for Visual Arts. title: Materials Lab Workshop: Making an Impression
description: Join assistant paper conservator Abby Schleicher and research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll discover how different printmaking techniques record both intentional design and the physical traces of making. Through hands-on experimentation using a variety of tools, pressures, inks, and papers, you’ll see how each technical choice leaves distinct traces—and why no two impressions are ever truly identical. We’ll look at a selection of prints under magnification and specialized conservation lighting to “read” their toolmarks, plate wear, inking, and condition. Linking studio experiments with close looking from a conservation perspective, this workshop will give you a concrete framework for identifying print processes and a richer appreciation of the material complexity of printed images. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! title: Materials Lab Workshop: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship
description: Join research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. We’ll explore the intimate connections between models, molds, and casts; how molds and casts have been used to produce, replicate, and preserve three-dimensional objects; and what these objects can teach us about skill, technology, and value. Working with clay, plaster, wax, alginate, and silicone putty, we’ll experiment with different processes of molding and casting. Along the way, you’ll be introduced to the scientific tools used to investigate and identify the traces of process and change. Through discussion and comparison with historical plaster casts, wax models, and other surrogates in the Harvard Art Museums collections, we’ll ask when a copy might be considered “fake,” “genuine,” or something in between, and how replicas support research, teaching, and conservation in museums today. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! title: The Material Culture of Islamic Calligraphy
description: The 2026 Norma Jean Calderwood Lecture Calligraphy is the most recognizable of Islamic arts, and it is often seen in its finished form—an inscription written on paper; carved in stone, wood, or ivory; cast in metal; or woven into fabric. Yet calligraphy always begins as a trace left by a pen, a practice sustained by a rich material culture. Cultural historian İrvin Cemil Schick looks at the wide array of tools used in the artistic practice of Islamic calligraphy, such as reed pens, penknives, cutting boards, inks, inkwells, papers, and scissors. Speaker: İrvin Cemil Schick, Cultural historian İrvin Cemil Schick is a cultural and intellectual historian specializing in the Ottoman Empire. He holds Ph.D.s from MIT and the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales, in Paris, and has taught at Harvard University, MIT, and Istanbul Şehir University. He has also held guest positions at Boston University, Sabancı University, Boğaziçi University, and the University of Massachusetts, Amherst. His principal research interests include the Islamic arts of the book, particularly calligraphy, illumination, and marbling; gender, sexuality, spatiality, and the body in Islam; animals and the environment in Islam; and occult practices in Islam. description: Join us to examine the relationship between suburban expansion and the history of redlining in the United States through postwar photography. title: Gallery Talk: The Gelatin Silver Print
description: Join photographs conservator Tatiana Cole for a discussion about the gelatin silver print—the most popular photographic process of the 20th century. title: Gallery Talk: Crafting Perfect Portraits with Photographic Proof Prints
description: Join Madison Brown, co-curator of The Way We Never Were: The American Professional Photographers Collection (August 29, 2026–May 9, 2027), for a discussion about the role of proof prints in the craft of producing polished studio portraits. Rather than capturing a single decisive moment behind the camera, the finished portrait is a result of a multi-step process. The proof prints are used by professional photographers to chart plans for retouching portraits, and photographers’ handwritten notations invite us to explore the extensive and collaborative work behind the sleek finished products. title: Frank Sriracha: Home is Where the Stage is
description: Frank Sriracha: Home is Where the Stage is Frank Sriracha is one of the most celebrated cabaret legends the world has ever seen. Tonight, he finally gets what he deserves: a Lifetime Achievement Award. Frank Sriracha has spent decades performing for crowds of adoring fans all over the European Black Box Circuit. But tonight, the Wonderkid of the Sunset Strip returns for his big award. First, Frank will give his big acceptance speech, and maybe sing a song. Then after like 5 or 10 minutes, everyone will get up and head to the massive gala reception with a fully catered Branzino dinner, open bar, and hundreds of dollars worth of free swag . So it’s only a five or ten minute speech in the theater, and then everyone will leave. But no one can leave until Frank gives his big speech, so it might be more like thirteen or eighteen minutes but there’s a huge free dinner after. Could be 20. title: Boston in 12 Massacres Part III
description: Boston in 12 Massacres Part III A four part, darkly humorous examination of how f***ed up Boston’s history can be, and how we used to just end each other’s lives all the time. Presented on September 15th, Part Three tells the stories of the nation’s most prolific female serial killer, Jane Toppan, the disaster of the Boston Molasses Flood, and the horrific Cocoanut Grove Fire in 1942. Local Storyteller and social media historian Daniel Berger-Jones recounts a scintillating, shocking, and irreverent narrative of the facts and then discusses them with a panel of local comedians, personalities, and performers. Audience members will have the opportunity to compete against the panel for $2 scratch lotto ticket prizes, or to sit passively and drink while being horrified and amused in an evening of history, ridicule, ribald toasts, drinking games, singing, and romping good times. All of this while discussing morbid violence, so if you’re easily offended, or a small and sensitive child, this show is not for you. This performance runs approximately 75 minutes. ARTIST BIO: Daniel Berger-Jones is a local actor, storyteller, tour guide, producer, and entrepreneur. As a founder of theatre company Orfeo Group and local tour outfit Boston History Company , his unique skills as a performer and public historian make his stories come alive. As a performer, he has been on stage with the Boston, Milwaukee , and Cincinnati Symphony Orchestras, the ART, Huntington Stage, Actors Shakespeare Project, Shakespeare and Co, Lyric Stage, Speakeasy Stage, Boston Playwright’s, Company One , and dozens of small but equally amazing companies around Boston. He is the host of the podcasts A People’s History of Food and Drink and the ribald history quiz show Get Shocked! with John J King . For daily short historic stories, follow him @bostonhistorycompany. SOCIAL MEDIA: @bostonhistorycompany (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube) Timeline: DOORS: 6:15 PM SHOW: 7:00 PM Age Limit: This event is All Ages

title: 2-Day Clown Intensive w Gemma Soldati
description: Clown Intensive w Gemma Soldati DESCRIPTION: Discover and reunite with your playful spirit and comedic vocabulary in this workshop of fun. Using clown, physical games, costume and improvisation, we’ll explore our imagination, pleasure, and our relationship with an audience. This workshop will help participants unleash their muse and confront their doubt. We’ll find what we may have lost or forgotten on our journey to become “good.” This class is for folks of all experience levels who are ready to take their comedic practice to the next level in a supportive and creative environment. IG: @Sleepyheadshow BIO: “Gemma’s absolute fearlessness matches her commitment to the absurd” – Comedy Bureau Gemma Soldati is an American performing and teaching artist. She won Best Comedy at the 2019 Melbourne Fringe with The Living Room. She has taught in Los Angeles, NYC, New England, Chicago, and Toronto for both adults and children. She was a 2023/24 resident at Ars Nova’s Makers Lab in NYC. Gemma’s focus is clown inspired work developed in front of live audiences. Her projects playfully dive deep into the heart of vital themes probing audiences with questions and meaning making – Grief, Ritual, Sleep, Dreams, Money, Power and beyond. Her current project is The Adventures of Sleepyhead, an all ages show, book and in-development tv program about a dreamer named Sleepyhead. DATES : September 19 & 20, 2026 DOORS : 9:30 AM START : 10:00 AM END : 3:00 PM AGES : 18+ TICKET PRICE : $200/250/300 CAPACITY : 16 The Rockwell is ADA Accessible. No refunds within 7 days of the workshop.

title: Jonathan Vale: Underground Magic
description: Some magicians pull rabbits from hats. Jonathan Vale pulls thoughts from your head. Enter the underground world of Jonathan Vale: where mind-reading, psychological illusions, and storytelling collide in a hypnotic journey that’s both intimate and dangerously convincing. Armed with little more than a deck of cards, a sharp wit, and a spellbinding gaze, Jonathan turns perception, fear, and dreams into an evening you can’t quite explain afterward. This isn’t a “tricky” show. Underground Magic is a mesmerizing descent into what’s real. You’ll witness impossible predictions, eerie coincidences, and deeply human storytelling, delivered with the friendly-yet-mysterious flair that’s made Jonathan a favorite across New England. You’ll laugh. You’ll gasp. You’ll leave wondering: How the **** did he do that? Come skeptical. Leave amazed. Artist Bio: Jonathan Vale is a magician, mentalist, and keynote speaker who blends mental-magic and life’s deep questions into performances that feel like glimpses into the mind. Creator of the one-man theater productions Magic Late at Night and Underground Magic, he’s taken the stage at TEDx, Fenway Park, Boston College, and for universities and corporate audiences across New England. In 2026, he appeared as a resident magician at The Hand and Eye in Chicago — one of the magic world’s most prestigious venues– for a multiple-show run to sold-out crowds. Instagram: @vale_mysteries www.valemysteries.com Jonathan Vale Magician and Mentalist- on Youtube and Facebook • Instagram: @vale_mysteries • TikTok: @JonathanVale • Facebook: Jonathan Vale – Magician & Mentalist This event is 21+ // Valid ID required for ENTRY Doors: 6:15 PM Show: 7:00 PM No refunds.

title: Brother Country
description: Brother Country SHOW DESCRIPTION: Brother Country is about two clown brothers embarking on a quixotic adventure across America. From the Wild West to 2001 September NYC, follow along this rollicking ranch romp as Lit and Robbie rob trains, play baseball with hotdogs, and do whatever it takes to save everything they ever thought about loving. This show uses clown and audience play to tackle themes of America and brotherhood. ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: @brothercountryclown ARTIST BIO: ANTIFA is real and it’s a clown duo started by Andrew Stout and Heschel Bay. Upon receiving critical acclaim, multiple tony awards and growing their company to Broadway and beyond, they felt unstoppable. Then the administration of the US changed in 2016. Their company’s success was taken from them, any records erased and they were banned from performing around the U.S. It was as if they never existed. Now, when the spirit of America seems to have been smothered by hate, they knew that Antifa had to return. After being banned and on the run the clown duo ANTIFA pilots a show you’ll #neverforget. title: “Be Good” with Paulette
description: “Be Good” with Paulette OH LOOK! HERE COMES THE MILDEST MAN IMAGINABLE. Paulette stumbles into a room full of the most strangers he’s ever seen, and he doesn’t know whether to panic or mingle—so he does both, for 60 minutes. Sporting a brown sweater and a hot-off-the-fist black eye, he dares to address the room armed with nothing but an arsenal of pleasantries and a monumental fear of rejection. Hot off of a high octane tour of Europe, the UK, and even the east coast of America, certified clown Daniel Maseda brings well-mannered idiot Paulette back to The Rockwell for the very second time with this fan-favorite show that never plays out the same way twice. A perfect evening for anyone who wants to scream at a polite person. Fringie Award (Clown), Philly Fringe 2025 Pick of the Fringe, Edinburgh Fringe 2025 (Mervyn Stutter) Best of the Fringe, District Fringe 2025 (DC Theater Arts) ★★★★½ “Utterly ridiculous…brilliantly performed…laugh-out-loud delirium.” (DC Theater Arts) ★★★★ “For this hour, just say yes to the madness.” (The Comic’s Comic) ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: IG @da.nee.ell ARTIST BIOS: Daniel Maseda (he/him) is a performer from Washington, DC who makes ridiculous work. He is currently touring his solo performance “BE GOOD!” WITH PAULETTE, which played at the 2025 Edinburgh Fringe (★★★★, Pick of the Fringe) and was awarded the inaugural Fringie for best Clown performance at the 2025 Philadelphia Fringe. Alongside his performance work, Daniel teaches workshops on clown, improvisation, and devising. He is a graduate of École Philippe Gaulier. title: Clown Class with Deby Xiadani
description: Clown Class With Deby Xiadani CLASS DESCRIPTION: Clown is an evergreen artform that is really having its moment! Find out why! Whether your a standup comedian, improvisor, expert clown, or have never done anything like this before, the art of CLOWN will unlock a new appreciation on life, performance, and laughter. This class is designed to make you a better performer, more sensitive to the audience, and a stronger artist. Open to all experience levels, this class offers a supportive and collaborative environment for anyone ready to elevate their comedic practice and rediscover what makes performing electric. 8-week session DATES: Sept. 28 Oct. 5 Oct. 12 (Indigenous Peoples’ Day) Oct. 19 Oct. 26 Nov. 2 Nov. 9 Nov. 16 TIME: Check-in: 5:45pm Class: 6pm-8:30pm COST: $400 / $450/ $500 for 8 classes, 2.5 hours each *Returning students (who have taken a 6-8 week class) are eligible for 20% off ($320 use code RETURNINGCLOWN) **Two work trade/skill share scholarships are available for new students. Email deby@therockwell.org to apply. MEET DEBY! Deby Xiadani is the Artistic Director of The Rockwell, as well as a director, comedian, writer, actor, and devisor passionate about creating bold new work. With a love for physical comedy rooted in a childhood obsession with Jim Carrey, Deby has developed a unique voice that blends playfulness, heart, and fearless experimentation. Her work has been recognized nationally: she directed Cooking with Kathryn, which won Best Physical Comedy at the FRIGID Fringe Festival and People’s Choice at PORTFringe. She also created the clown show Miss Route 1 for the Boston Fringe and founded the Boston Fringe Festival itself, building a platform for boundary-pushing performance. In addition to her original work, Deby has assistant directed Off-Broadway and continues to champion emerging artists while developing her own inventive projects that challenge and delight audiences. www.debyx.com @debyxiadani on insta

title: Jaboukie Young-White
description: Jaboukie Young – White ARTIST BIO: Jaboukie Young-White is a comedian, writer, filmmaker, and musician from Chicago who was a correspondent on THE DAILY SHOW WITH TREVOR NOAH. Named one of Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch at the 2018 Just for Laughs Montreal Comedy Festival, Jaboukie has performed stand up twice on THE TONIGHT SHOW STARRING JIMMY FALLON and debuted his half-hour comedy special on COMEDY CENTRAL STAND-UP PRESENTS. Jaboukie’s writing credits include Netflix’s AMERICAN VANDAL and BIG MOUTH. He can be seen in the last season of HBO’s CRASHING, recurring in the Hulu series ONLY MURDERS IN THE BUILDING, recurring in the HBO Max series RAP SH!T, produced by Issa Rae, and as a guest star of Netflix’s BLACK MIRROR. On the feature side, you can see him in the A24 produced Mike Mills feature C’MON, C’MON opposite Joaquin Phoenix, Sony’s ROUGH NIGHT directed by Lucia Aniello, Netflix’s SET IT UP directed by Claire Scanlon, SOMEONE GREAT directed by Jennifer Kaytin Robinson, and as the lead in the film DATING & NEW YORK, released by IFC Films. Jaboukie also voices the lead roles of “Truman” in the animated series FAIRFAX on Amazon, and the role of “Ethan” in Disney’s STRANGE WORLD. Most recently, Jaboukie can be seen in THE THREESOME, directed by Chad Hartigan, which just premiered at SXSW 2025 and the Warner Brothers feature film, COMPANION, directed by Drew Hancock, now streaming. Jaboukie’s musical debut, All Who Can’t Hear Must Feel, was released through Interscope records in 2023. He currently recurs and writes on ABC’s ABBOTT ELEMENTARY. title: The Schizophonics
description: The Schizophonics Amps screaming. No exit in sight. The Schizophonics kick the door in and never let it close. This San Diego–based three-piece delivers a live show that’s loud and dangerously fun—an all-gas, no-brakes blast of feedback and groove. It’s full-contact rock ’n’ roll: high voltage, high velocity, and sharpened to a blade. The band features Pat Beers on vocals and guitar, Lety Beers on drums, and Sarah Linton on bass. Together they unleash a fuzz-soaked, funk-fueled attack built on pounding rhythm and feral energy. Every song hits like a charge. Every set feels like the floor might give out. Blink and you miss something. Stand still and you get run over. Forged on the road and fueled by motion, The Schizophonics have torn through stages in fourteen countries, earning a reputation as a must-see live act that turns rooms upside down. Channeling the raw spirit of James Brown, Iggy Pop, Jimi Hendrix, Little Richard, and The Sonics, they strip rock back to its most dangerous elements—and set them loose. — Schizophonics Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: This show is all ages. title: The Commute
description: The Commute SHOW DESCRIPTION: Four strangers are trapped in a tunnel during a sudden stop on the Red Line. As tension builds, they are forced to confront each other-and themselves. The Commute is a dark, thought provoking new comedy by Karin Anell, exploring human behavior under pressure. Who are we really, behind our masks? The evening show will be followed by an interactive talk-back and panel discussing the evolving role of technology in our lives. ARTIST STATEMENT: “I love listening to people’s life stories. My scripts are often based on individuals’ lived experiences and I believe in theatre as a powerful vehicle to bring these engaging narratives to life. Theatre can bring people together to start important conversations, and I don’t mean discussions around who was the better actor, or whether the third act was too long. I want people to leave the theatre and spend the next couple of hours discussing what they saw. How did this piece make them feel? What are they thinking right now? Did this play open their eyes to something new; see the world, and themselves, in a different light? I like to include interactive sessions with a subject matter expert(s) after performances. I moderate these sessions, inviting the audience to participate and ask questions about what they saw. Themes I have brought to life include a mother’s guilt, body image, and our biggest fears. It does not take a million-dollar production that runs for 3 hours to engage an audience and stimulate an interesting debate. I believe in: Simplicity and adaptability-use modern technology to make theatre more engaging and entertaining Short plays that pack a punch, using local talent Community-based theatre accessible to all” — Karin Anell SOCIAL MEDIAS: Facebook: tcsquaredthea tre / Instagram: @tc2theatre Timeline: EARLY SHOW: DOORS: 12:30 PM SHOW: 1:00 PM LATE SHOW (With Panel!): DOORS: 6:15 PM SHOW: 7:00 PM Age Limit: This event is All Ages ID: Valid ID required for Alcohol Consumption Limited Late

title: The TUNEabomber
description: The TUNEabomber SHOW DESCRIPTION: Set at a parole board hearing, Ted Kaczynski (aka The Unabomber) recounts his life through song in the hope of proving that he never wanted to be a monster, he only wanted to be a star. While he may have spent years sending explosives, this is one performance Ted can’t bomb. Written and performed by John Lampe and Michael Wysong, this new musical comedy dares to ask the question no one needed an answer to: What if this notorious eco-terrorist was the next Bob Fosse? ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: @thetuneabomber ARTIST BIOS: Michael Wysong is a Manhattan-based musical theatre composer and lyricist who was described by Cabaret Scenes as “a wry and clever songwriter and political satirist in the tradition of Tom Lehrer…a major talent to be kept track of.” His work has been performed at cabaret venues and theatres throughout New York City, including the Triad Theatre and Feinstein’s/54 Below. Recent credits include new music for a production of Marat/Sade, music and sound design for Macbeth (New York Shakespeare Company), and music and sound design for Aunt Jack (Theater for the New City). He also wrote the book and lyrics for a new adaptation of The Revenger’s Tragedy, music and lyrics for the song cycle Love is…, and contributed a song to CHANGEMAKERS with Tony Nominated lyricist Bill Russell for their shared alma mater, The University of Kansas. John Lampe is a director, writer, and performer. His work has been seen across the US and in Europe. In New York, he has worked with companies such as Urban Stages, New Circle Theatre, Frog and Peach Theatre, and ANDTheatre, where he served as Artistic Director. His two man musical comedy “The TUNEabomber” plays monthly in New York at The Reverie Room. Keep in touch at www.johnlampe.com . description: Tame Your Inner Critic: A Live Book Launch & Interactive Workshop with Caitlin Green What becomes possible when you stop believing your inner critic? Join author and self-trust coach Caitlin Green for an inspiring and interactive evening celebrating the launch of her debut book, Tame Your Inner Critic . Come for the book. Leave with a new relationship with yourself. title: Voices Unheard
description: Voices Unheard SHOW DESCRIPTION: Voices Unheard: From the Margins to the Mic returns to Massachusetts for its seventh consecutive year, continuing its tradition of centering lived experience through story. The event features true narratives from adult storytellers who have submitted their work, sharing personal accounts of identity, origin, separation, and reunion. While participants come from a range of lived experiences—including adoption, foster care, donor conception, and unexpected family discoveries—the lineup reflects those who have chosen to step forward and share their stories this year. Together, these voices create a collective portrait of what it means to grow up without full access to one’s origins, and the ongoing search for connection, meaning, and belonging. ARTIST BIO: Lisa “LC” Coppola is a domestic DCF adoptee, writer, educator, and creator of the Voices Unheard Storytelling Program. She is the author of Voices Unheard: A Reflective Journal for Adult Adoptees and the essay Heartichoke, featured in the 2026 anthology Relative Strangers: Inheritance, Identity, and the Meaning of Kinship. Her debut novel, Monster Flower, is forthcoming from Jaded Ibis Press in Spring 2027. Kristal Parke is a talented filmmaker, producer, speaker and podcaster whose work explores identity, belonging, and resilience. A transracial adoptee from a closed adoption, her personal journey fuels her storytelling with authenticity, compassion, and truth. She creates space for unheard voices, shaping narratives that educate, challenge, inspire and heal. title: Infrastructure in a Time of Flux: Actions in Public Exhibition Opening
description: We are living through a moment of dramatic environmental, social, political, and technological change. Yet, architecture, urban design, and planning still tend to imagine permanence, rather than embrace change—favoring stability and order, and treating transformation as something to manage, rather than a force that can shape the future. The exhibition,Infrastructure in a Time of Flux: Methods, Conditions, and Situations,curated by Rahul Mehrotra and Dan Borelli, brings together architectural, engineering, planning, and design ideas whose potential has yet to be fully realized. This opening event celebrates the power of art to bring these questions to life. Join us for an evening that begins with a guided walk-through of the gallery, led by the exhibition’s curators, followed by a screening of a clip from the documentary filmRunning Fence(directed by Albert Maysles, David Maysles, and Charlotte Zwerin, 1977),about Christo and Jeanne-Claude’s installation. After the screening, Vladimir Yavachev, director of operations at the Christo and Jeanne-Claude Foundation, and Antoine Picon will join the curators to discuss the film and its legacy. This exhibition is supported by the Koji Yanai Innovative Infrastructure Initiative Fund. This event is part ofArtsThursdays, a university-wide initiative supported by the Harvard University Committee on the Arts (HUCA).
