title: Golden Rose Award (Poetry): Marie Howe
description: The Longfellow Summer Arts Festival brings music, poetry, and community to the East Lawn of the Longfellow House on Sunday afternoons through the summer. All events are free and open to the public. This reading is presented in partnership with the New England Poetry Club. Marie Howe, recipient of the 2026 Golden Rose Award for Poetry, is the author of New and Selected Poems, (W.W. Norton 2024.) which includes poems from her four previous books. From 2012-2014, she served as the Poet Laureate of New York State. She is the poet in residence at The Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine, and a chancellor of the Academy of American Poets. Marie Howe's The Good Thief (1988), was chosen for the National Poetry Series by Margaret Atwood, who praised Howe’s “poems of obsession that transcend their own dark roots.” In that collection, Howe’s oracular yet self-doubting speakers often voice their concerns through Biblical and mythical allusions. Kunitz, on selecting the book for the Lavan Younger Poets Prize from the American Academy of Poets, observed, “Her long, deep-breathing lines address the mysteries of flesh and spirit, in terms accessible only to a woman who is very much of our time and yet still in touch with the sacred.” Howe has taught at Sarah Lawrence College, Columbia University, and NYU. She coedited (with Michael Klein) the essay anthology In the Company of My Solitude: American Writing from the AIDS Pandemic (1994). She has received fellowships from the Bunting Institute at Radcliffe College, the National Endowment for the Arts, the Guggenheim Foundation, the Academy of American Poets, and the Fine Arts Work Center in Provincetown. She was the Poet Laureate of New York State from 2012 to 2014. She is the poet in residence at The Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine and a chancellor of the Academy of American Poets. Howe lives in New York City.

After moving to the United States, she continued her studies at Berklee College of Music with the support of a Presidential Scholarship. She has performed at Panama Jazz Festival, Medford Jazz Festival, Boston Progressive Jazz Festival, and a variety of venues in Korea and Boston. She was featured as an emerging artist at the 2024 Vermont Solo Jazz Piano Festival.

As a founding member of Grupo los Santos (Santos4tet), a vanguard Afro-Cuban and Brazilian-style quartet, he has played New York’s Town Hall and concerts throughout the U.S., Cuba & Austria. In 2024, Santos4tet was the recipient of a JazzRoad Touring Grant from SouthArts, funded by the Doris Duke Foundation and the Mellon Foundation, which supported their 5-city tour of the Sountheast. title: Elizabeth Margulis at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Elizabeth Margulis —Professor and Acting Chair of the Department of Music at Princeton University, where she directs the Music Cognition Lab—for a discussion of her new book, Transported: The Everyday Magic of Musical Daydreams. She will be joined in conversation by Psyche Loui —Associate Professor of Creativity and Creative Practice in the Department of Music at Northeastern University, where she directs the MIND (Music, Imaging, and Neural Dynamics) Lab. About Transported A song comes on—and suddenly, you’re somewhere else. Reliving past heartbreak. Picturing a serene future. Imagining a fantastical scene. Across genres, music has an uncanny ability to carry us into distinct inner worlds. In Transported , acclaimed music cognition researcher Elizabeth Margulis explores the phenomenon of musical daydreams —the vivid, spontaneous, emotionally charged images, stories, and memories we lapse into while listening to music—and argues that these everyday reveries offer a powerful and underappreciated window into how we think, feel, and connect. Combining cutting-edge neuroscience, psychology, ethnography, and revelations from her own teaching and pathbreaking research, Margulis shows not only that musical imaginings are widespread and meaningful—but also that daydreams which seem deeply personal are often widely shared. Music can alleviate anxiety, ignite creativity, and foster connection in our increasingly fragmented era. At a time when attention is perpetually under siege, Transported makes a powerful case for music as one of the last spaces where the mind is still free to wander—and reminds us that these wanderings are more meaningful and more important to our individual and collective well-being than we’ve ever realized. Praise for Transported "Margulis writes in an easy, conversational style, never solemnly scholarly, and raises as many enticing questions as she answers. title: Mark Peterson at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Mark Peterson —Edmund S. Morgan Professor of History at Yale University and the Faculty Director of Yale’s Lewis Walpole Library—for a discussion of his book, The Making and Breaking of the American Constitution: A Thousand-Year History. He will be joined in conversation by Emilie Connolly —Assistant Professor of History at Yale University and the award-winning author of Vested Interests . About The Making and Breaking of the American Constitution A provocative new history of America’s constitution and an urgent call to action for a nation confronted by challenges its founders could never have imagined. The American Revolution occurred at a time when Britain’s constitutional order failed to adapt to the extraordinary growth of its colonies. The framers designed an American constitution to succeed where Britain’s had faltered, planning for continuous population and territorial expansion that would eventually cross the continent. Yet by the end of the nineteenth century, it was already ill-suited for an increasingly urban, industrialized society, and the transformations of the twentieth century have pushed it to a breaking point. This book charts the history and aims of the American constitution from its origins in an agrarian past to the grave crisis we face today. Mark Peterson traces the American constitutional tradition to the control of land in medieval England, showing how the founders incorporated the aspirations of Magna Carta with the administrative principles of the Domesday Book, a meticulous survey and valuation of landed property commissioned by William the Conqueror. This framework encouraged the growth of democratic self-government in a young nation. It also institutionalized the colonization of territory and the expulsion of Indigenous peoples, establishing a legal blueprint for transforming tribal lands into revenue-yielding real estate for settlers. Peterson’s riveting narrative paints an arresting picture of a dynamic rep

title: Christopher M. Finan at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Christopher M. Finan —former executive director of the National Coalition Against Censorship and the former president of the American Booksellers Foundation for Free Expression—for a discussion of his new book Freedom of Speech: A People’s History of Democracy’s Most Essential Right. He will be joined in conversation by Randall Kennedy —Michael R. Klein Professor at Harvard Law School and the author of Say It Loud!: On Race, Law, History, and Culture. About Freedom of Speech An essential look at how, throughout American history, the powerless have exercised their 1st Amendment right to free speech, informing how we can defend democracy today, with a forward by Randall Kennedy. From the beginning of American history, free speech has been crucial for the pursuit of justice and expansion of democracy. Yet today, we are seeing growing attempts to roll back free speech protections in America: cultural warriors are banning books from library shelves at a level not seen in decades, and elected officials are attacking free speech principles to undermine other rights and consolidate their own power. Uncovering vivid and engaging stories about 1st Amendment pioneers throughout American history, historian and leading censorship expert Christopher Finan highlights how free speech has been used to advocate for change. In the 19th century, abolitionists, advocates for women's rights, and leaders of the labor movement had to fight for free speech. In the 20th century, the civil rights and anti-war movements expanded free speech, creating a shield for every protest movement that we have seen since. With sharp insight and page-turning storytelling, Finan demonstrates that the most effective antidote for the growth of hate speech, misinformation, political violence, and anti-democratic efforts by government officials is support for and cultivation of a free and robust marketplace of ideas. Praise for Freedom of Speech "Great storytelling about the history

title: Roshan Sethi at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Roshan Sethi —award-winning writer, director, and practicing oncologist—for a discussion of his debut book The Simp: A Novel Without a Hero, about the rise and fall of an unemployed actor who lands the greatest role of his life when he's hired as a personal assistant to a demanding, highly absurd Hollywood family. He will be joined in conversation by Daphne Kalotay —acclaimed author of The Archivists and Calamity and Other Stories , and Special Program Instructor in the Masters in Creative Writing & Literature Program at Harvard University's Division of Continuing Education. About The Simp A razor-sharp novel about the rise and fall of an unemployed actor who lands the greatest role of his life when he’s hired as a personal assistant to an absurd Hollywood family. Raj Ladlani is a morose and unemployable actor. He has reasons to believe he is spectacularly talented, a legend in every way but for the success. He leads an anonymous life in LA, working part time at a frozen yogurt store, fantasizing about stardom and clinging to the encouragement of his aging and kindly acting coach. At his life's nadir, Raj reads a job posting detailing a relentless, laughable parade of menial responsibilities for an organization blandly described as “Hollywood Family.” The Simp tells the story of Raj’s momentous employment with the H Family and the destruction that follows. Jim H is a massive and macho director in a creative rut. Anna H might uncharitably be described as his much younger trophy wife, quietly and neurotically seeking out her own independent sense of purpose as a screenwriter. Raj’s work as their executive assistant becomes his new sense of soaring purpose. But he procured the job through a sea of lies. The job itself is an absurdist walk through a landmine of affluent domestic chaos, identity politics, and petty Angeleno grievances. And things only get weirder when it turns out Anna H has been working on a secret project of her own—one that

title: Rowan Jacobsen at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store, the Harvard University Division of Science, and the Harvard Library welcome Rowan Jacobsen —acclaimed author of nine books, including A Geography of Oysters , Fruitless Fall , and Truffle Hound —for a discussion of his latest book In Defense of Sunlight: The Surprising Science of Sun Exposure. About In Defense of Sunlight Upending everything we thought we knew about sun exposure, this trenchant investigation into the “zero-sun policy” sounds the call on the many health benefits of the sun, and what we risk when we minimize our exposure. A quiet revolution is transforming our understanding of sunlight’s effects on human health. For decades, a “zero-sun” policy has characterized our approach to sun protection, advising us to stay out of the sun whenever possible and apply sunscreen daily to any skin that might be exposed, rain or shine, summer or winter, indoors or out. But recent studies have proved that this policy is thoroughly mistaken and that this prolific misunderstanding is causing us to miss out on many of the health benefits of sun exposure. In this incisive work, acclaimed journalist Rowan Jacobsen presents the growing case for the importance of modest sun exposure for our health and well-being. Aided by the most up-to-date studies on the effects of sunlight on human health, Jacobsen presents a much-needed, lucid assessment of not only what the sun can do for us, but how a lack of sun could actively be harming us. In Defense of Sunlight sounds the call on what researchers have been sure of for years, and what health care providers and media outlets have been slow to take up: that sunlight is one of the simplest, and most equitable, treatments for a variety of health issues, from diabetes to dementia to multiple sclerosis. Laying out the new science of sunlight in a straightforward and responsible manner for mainstream readers, this book is an eye-opening story of scientific discovery, outlining not only best practices for sun exposure, b

title: Howard A. Rodman at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Howard A. Rodman —a vice president of the Academy for Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and one of seventeen members of the Screenwriters Hall of Fame—for a discussion of his novels Destiny Express and The Great Eastern. He will be joined in conversation by Sam Marks —award-winning playwright, television writer, and Senior Lecturer on Playwriting at Harvard University. About Destiny Express Hailed by Thomas Pynchon as “daringly imagined and darkly romantic—a moral thriller,” Destiny Express captures both the glamour and the terror of an era, dramatizing the perilous moment when art, politics, and destiny converged on the tracks out of Berlin. Berlin, the last day of February, 1933. The Reichstag lies in smoldering ruins, a new world about to spring from its ashes. And now for German filmmakers the choices are stark: stay and collaborate with a government that believes in cinema’s power to shape reality, or leave everything behind. Destiny Express is the story of Fritz Lang and Thea von Harbou, husband and wife, director and screenwriter—together, they made some of the greatest films of all time: M, Metropolis, Doctor Mabuse. As each day is torn from the calendar they watch as one by one Bertolt Brecht, Max Ophuls, Billy Wilder, take the next train out. Destiny Express follows Lang, von Harbou, and a host of real and fictional others––novelist-turned-minister-of-culture Joseph Goebbels, American café Surrealist Sam Harrison, Mercedes racing champ Otto Merz, film star Rudolf Klein-Rogge, a pair of not-so-secret police—as their paths converge, intertwine, and separate across the grid of Berlin, from the artificial daylight of the UFA soundstage to the artificial night of Berlin's most exclusive and decadent nightclubs. title: Chloe Chapin at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Chloe Chapin —American historian, costume designer, and fashion scholar—for a discussion of her new book, Suitable: The Sartorial Revolution and the Fashioning of Modern Men. She will be joined in conversation by Michelle Finamore —fashion & design Curator, author, and historian who was previously Curator of Fashion Arts at the Museum of Fine Arts. About Suitable How did black suits become so ubiquitous? Why has men's clothing been so plain since the American Revolution? In Suitable , American historian and costume designer Chloe Chapin offers a deeply researched and groundbreaking explanation for why American men's fashion was standardized from the time of the nation's founding and how it became an invisible form of social and political power. The surprising story of how the plain black suit became a symbol of masculinity, democracy, and modernity. How did black suits become so ubiquitous? Why has men's business clothing been so plain for the last 250 years? How did a style adopted by the Founding Fathers to differentiate themselves from European contemporaries become the dominant style for men around the globe? Suitable traces the shift from the colorful, flamboyant attire of the eighteenth century to the plain dark suit of the nineteenth century, characterizing this style evolution as a "Sartorial Revolution." In this book, American historian and costume designer Chloe Chapin traces the evolution of masculine style from the American Revolution through the Civil War and shows how men's suits shaped relationships of gender and power. Drawing on a wealth of visual and written sources, she shows how the plainness of suits symbolized new ideals of rationality and democracy and played a crucial role in framing the lasting identity and authority of American men. This richly illustrated book analyzes fashion history's impact on gender dynamics and emphasizes the dynamic relationships between bodies, clothing, and personal identity. Suitable de

title: Carson Markland at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Carson Markland —acclaimed writer and filmmaker from South Carolina featured in the Best Microfiction Anthology —for a discussion of her debut novel, Men Like Us . She will be joined in conversation by Brian Castleberry —acclaimed author of Nine Shiny Objects and The Californians. About Men Like Us The surprising, poignant Kennedy story you don't know, with the enigmatic Bobby Kennedy at its heart. Bobby Kennedy was never meant to matter. The seventh of nine children, he’s long been overlooked by his father, Joseph P. Kennedy, Sr., who governs his children with the same firm hand that earned him a fortune, an ambassadorship, and enough clout to plant the seeds of an American political dynasty. But when Bobby’s eldest brother, the anointed heir, dies in a wartime mission, the burden to become the first Kennedy in Congress shifts to Jack, the next in line. Bobby—long ignored and underestimated—is forced to step up, especially as debilitating chronic pain threatens Jack’s Senate seat and aspirations to higher office. With their sights eventually set on the White House, Bobby evolves into the ruthless operative behind the scenes—yet at what personal cost? Throughout the chaos of campaign after campaign, Bobby finds an unexpected ally in his brother’s wife, Jacqueline Bouvier. While Jackie smiles and waves for the cameras, in private, she leans on Bobby for understanding. Their friendship serves as a refuge from the public spotlight and private intrigue of the Kennedy family, but Jack’s ongoing infidelity tests the boundaries of their loyalty, forcing Bobby and Jackie to each decide just how much they’re willing to sacrifice for the dynasty’s image. Centering on one of the most significant political families of our time, Carson Markland’s riveting, hopeful debut is about brothers, fathers and sons, winners and losers, loyalty and sacrifice, and the true cost of power. title: P.C. Verrone at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes P.C. Verrone —award-winning writer whose work has appeared in FIYAH and PodCastle —for a discussion of his debut novel, Rabbit, Fox, Tar, a Debutiful "Most Anticipated Book of the Year". He will be joined in conversation by Linda Schlossberg —Associate Director of the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Program at Harvard University and author of the novel Life in Miniature. About Rabbit, Fox, Tar A mesmerizing, fable-like debut novel about a mysterious young Black woman whose arrival in an insular neighborhood threatens to shake its foundations. When Baby appears in Original Hill, her name is on everyone's lips. A young Black woman is a rare sight in this part of town, and she sits all day on the Foxes’ garden wall, swinging her bare feet and speaking to no one. That is, until the charismatic Lucius “Lucky” Foote comes along and touches her, sparking their romance. Arm-in-arm with Baby, who seems to exert a seemingly supernatural pull on the other residents, Lucky is confident he will secure the open city council seat away from Baby’s uncle Eugene Fox, the back-from-retirement white incumbent. With protestors reopening old wounds around the Black neighborhood that was leveled by the nearby highway decades ago and Lucky threatening his position, Fox believes it’s not just a city council seat at stake, but the “soul” of Original Hill. As Baby is woven further into the unraveling community, she begins to stray from Fox’s strict rules and question everything, from where she came from to who—and what—she truly is. Praise for Rabbit, Fox, Tar "Verrone's sparkling reworking of American folklore's tar baby tale compels, haunts and delights all at once—a remarkable debut!" —Claire Messud, author of This Strange Eventful History "P.C. Verrone’s debut novel Rabbit, Fox, Tar is as haunting as it is enchanting. title: Julia Skinner at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Dr. Julia Skinner —award-winning author of Our Fermented Lives , culinary business owner, writing coach, and food historian—for a discussion of her new book, Essential Food Preserving: The Comprehensive Guide to Canning, Freezing, Drying, and Fermenting Vegetables, Fruits, Grains, Nuts, Beans, Meat, Dairy, and Eggs. She will be joined in conversation by Andrew Janjigian —head baker at the IACP-nominated Wordloaf newsletter, author of The Bread Baker’s Pocket Companion and Breaducation , and the inventor of the sourdough starter whisk. About Essential Food Preserving The must-have reference guide to all the methods used for preserving every type of food—from canning vegetables to making fruit wines to curing meat—with more than 250 recipes and creative zero-waste options. Featuring clear step-by-step instructions and original photography, Essential Food Preserving is organized by type of food, with multiple preservation methods for each one, so you can preserve almost anything in a variety of ways, including: Canning Fermenting Brewing beer, wine, and vinegar Pickling Making jams and jellies Drying Smoking Cold storage Food-preserving expert Julia Skinner focuses on minimizing waste; every part is used, including the byproducts of processes. Just as important as her comprehensive approach is Julia’s expert curation of the topic and creative recipes that go beyond the basics. Praise for Essential Food Preserving “Essential Food Preserving is extraordinary! For Julia Skinner, preserving is a way of life, a pathway to exciting new flavors, personal wellbeing, and sustainable eating. Julia shares the collective wisdom she’s gleaned from ancient preserving techniques around the world while offering her own innovative spins on classic recipes, especially for fermentation. She addresses every question you might ever have about how to preserve food safely and deliciously. This comprehensive volume is destined to become the go-to reference for mode

title: July Harvard Square Book Circle
description: Join us for our July Harvard Square Book Circle meeting! This month we're discussing My Friends: A Novel by Hisham Matar. Don't forget each book we discuss is part of our featured Select 70 for frequent buyer members . The Book Circle is Harvard Book Store's monthly book club open for members of the community to meet and discuss a thoughtfully selected book. We’ll meet in the third room of the store from 6–7:30 PM. Registration is not required and no commitment is necessary. We love new participants! If you are interested in joining the Book Circle's email list, sign up through this form . Obsessed by the power of those words—and by their enigmatic author, Hosam Zowa—Khaled eventually embarks on a journey that will take him far from home, to pursue a life of the mind at the University of Edinburgh. There, thrust into an open society that is miles away from the world he knew in Libya, Khaled begins to change. He attends a protest against the Qaddafi regime in London, only to watch it explode into tragedy. In a flash, Khaled finds himself injured, clinging to life, unable to leave Britain, much less return to the country of his birth. To even tell his mother a

title: Danielle Allen at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Danielle Allen —James Bryant Conant University Professor at Harvard University and author of Justice by Means of Democracy, Cuz , and Our Declaration —for a discussion of her new book, Radical Duke: How One Aristocrat-and the American Revolution-Transformed Britain . She will be joined in conversation by Eric Nelson —Robert M. Beren Professor of Government at Harvard University and a Senior Fellow in the Society of Fellows. About Radical Duke An explosive, deeply revisionist work that reveals how a renegade English Duke and Thomas Paine, the firebrand polemicist, almost brought the American Revolution to Britain. When Danielle Allen unearthed a parchment of the Declaration of Independence buried away in Sussex, England, little did she know that she had discovered a story of historical magnitude that would alter our understanding of British and American history. Revealing that the Age of Revolution began earlier than we thought—not with the Boston patriots nor with the Parisian Jacobins, but in Britain itself—Allen demonstrates in Radical Duke that the rights of man, the theory of revolution, and calls for popular sovereignty all emerged from the radical energies of London before they spread across the Atlantic and the Channel. At the center of this new age was Charles Lennox, the progressive Third Duke of Richmond, a rarely cited historical figure who becomes the biographical focus of Allen’s groundbreaking work. Even with royal blood coursing through his veins, the handsome, gallivanting Duke (1735–1806) preferred to rub shoulders with ordinary folk—supporting the rights of jurors, freedom of the press, and religious toleration. As Allen shows, from 1767 to 1782, he was England’s leading voice of opposition to the Crown, and, as the leader of the Sussex militia, even a threat to the King’s power. But the Duke did not challenge the Crown alone. The archives have long hidden the covert alliance between the young Duke and his age-mate Thoma

title: John A. Jenkins at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes John A. Jenkins —multi-award-winning journalist, author, publisher, and entrepreneur—for a discussion of his new book, Summer of '71: Five Months That Changed America . He will be joined in conversation by Hilary Braseth —executive director of OpenSecrets. About Summer of '71 From award-winning journalist and author John A. Jenkins comes a revolutionary exploration of the summer before Watergate—a parallel world of a half-century ago when America faced events and crises strikingly similar to those of today—told through the lives and words of those who lived it. Inflation rages. Crime is rising. Abortion rights take center stage at the Supreme Court. China poses an existential threat. Black lives are under attack. The president battles the press as he seeks to subvert not just the political order but the rule of law itself. This is the Summer of ’71 —a pivotal, operatic season of hope and despair, missed opportunities and era-changing decisions. More than a half-century later, it’s difficult to overstate the importance of events that defined the American experience during that fateful five-month period spanning May to September 1971. On May Day, President Nixon orchestrates a massive police-military response to disrupt the biggest anti-war demonstration in history. Two days later, the Supreme Court announces that it will take up Roe v. Wade. In the weeks and months that follow, friction escalates between the police and the Black Panthers, Congress debates universal healthcare, Attica prisoners riot, and the New York Times publishes the Pentagon Papers—a turning point that ultimately dooms Nixon’s presidency and his legacy. Summer of ’71 brings it all to the page through first-person accounts that are only now becoming available: the papers, diaries, and oral histories of key players. title: Ben Wikler at the Cambridge Public Library
description: RSVP is required for this event. He will be joined in conversation by Danielle Allen —James Bryant Conant University Professor at Harvard University, acclaimed author of Our Declaration , and the forthcoming book Radical Duke , releasing June 2026. This offer expires after 30 days. Please note we cannot guarantee signed copies will be available to ticket holders who do not attend the event. Ben Wikler led the Democratic Party of Wisconsin to a string of improbable victories in a state with a political system so rigged that it was dubbed a “democracy desert”—which is, coincidentally, Trump’s goal for the whole country. title: Yotam Marom at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Yotam Marom —leading activist, organizer, and co-founder of IfNotNow and the Wildfire Project—for a discussion of his debut book, For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness . He will be joined in conversation by Marshall Ganz —Rita E. Hauser Senior Lecturer in Leadership, Organizing and Civil Society at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government, and the author of People, Power, Change: Organizing for Democratic Renewal . About For Louder Days The essential guide to establishing an effective opposition movement in the age of Trump, from the leading activist and organizer . There is no way to stop the descent into authoritarianism, nor win a world in which all people can thrive, without massive numbers of people organizing for social, political, and economic change. Yet experienced movement leader Yotam Marom delivers a hard truth: progressive and left movements too often get in their own way. They can be ambivalent about power, choosing insularity and purity over winning. This amounts to what Marom calls the “politics of powerlessness,” which has kept movements small, weak, and defeated. In For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness , Marom offers a brilliant, lyrical clarion cry for a more honest, more strategic, more loving approach to progressive activism and movement building. Grounded in decades of experience in movements, from leading at Occupy Wall Street and other movement moments to supporting some of the most important climate, racial justice, and democracy movements of our time, Marom dives deep into the challenges that hold movements back, and offers stories, tools, and paths toward real power and enduring change. Published at the most perilous time in our modern political history, For Louder Days comes not a moment too soon. It is essential reading for committed activists as well as the wider public concerned about the state of our world and hoping to change it for the better. Praise for For

title: Meg Richardson at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Meg Richardson —writer, translator, and cartoonist from Iowa—for a discussion of her debut novel, Paradise Pawn , based on her experiences working behind the counter of a pawn shop. She will be joined in conversation by Hannah Kauders —local writer and translator who teaches in the Harvard College Writing Program. About Paradise Pawn A dazzling debut novel about best friends, adolescent longing, and the Florida pawn shop that promises to make their dreams come true—if it doesn’t break them apart first. Fall in love with Paradise Pawn , Meg Richardson’s debut novel based on her own experiences working behind the counter of a pawn shop. Teenage best friends Jackie and Kayla can sell anything. Alongside their fathers, they work at a pawn shop in Cherry Beach, Florida, handling everything from Cartier jewelry to chainsaws to cars. When the girls learn that Kayla’s family can’t afford a private school opportunity that Jackie’s can, Jackie becomes distraught about losing her best friend if they go to different schools. With their sharp minds but youthful lack of foresight, they scheme a way to embezzle money from the pawn shop. As the hot Florida summer unfolds, the girls steal thousands of dollars from the shop. But when their heist is discovered, Jackie is faced with a situation that no amount of negotiating or charisma can fix. With incredible heart and wit, Richardson navigates current-day themes of trust, familial love, female friendship, and class differences, and asks us how far we would go to protect the ones we love most. Praise for Paradise Pawn “ Paradise Pawn introduces us to a world that feels deeply lived in, and Meg Richardson gets every detail just right. In the pawn shop, we are privy to the pendulum of human desperation: what people need and what they're willing to sacrifice. The friendship between Jackie and Kayla perfectly captures the feeling of being caught between: between new friends and old friends that feel like family

title: Elizabeth Stordeur Pryor at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Elizabeth Stordeur Pryor —professor of history at Smith College where she teaches courses on race, slavery, and one on her father, comedic legend Richard Pryor—for a discussion of her new memoir, Something We Said: Richard Pryor, a Notorious Word, and Me. She will be joined in conversation by Kellie Carter Jackson —Michael and Denise Kellen ‘68 Associate Professor of Africana Studies and the Chair of the Africana Studies Department Wellesley College, and the award winning author of We Refuse and Force & Freedom . About Something We Said Part memoir by the daughter of the iconic comedian Richard Pryor, part exploration of the historical and contemporary use of the N-word, this hybrid book peels back the curtain on the life of Pryor and interrogates the most perplexing word in the American lexicon, a word he helped popularize. The N-word is one of the most perplexing, controversial and misunderstood words in the American lexicon. It’s a word that Elizabeth Pryor has not only contemplated, it’s one that she has taught and observed up close. When a white student quoted her father and blurted out the N-word in the middle of a class she was teaching, Professor Pryor’s worlds collided. In that moment, she was forced to confront the history of the notorious slur in the United States, and her complicated relationship with her father Richard Pryor, who made the word a trademark of his comedy in the 1970s. As she dives into her research, her own memories of the N-word come flooding back in unprocessed memories that she hadn’t thought about for decades. In reckoning with those memories, Elizabeth goes on a more public journey of discovery of the messy and sometimes surprising legacies of racism in the United States. A braided narrative that seamlessly integrates the history of the N-word with Elizabeth’s own story of growing up the Black Jewish daughter of Richard Pryor, Something We Said follows Elizabeth as she becomes a leading scholar and teacher

title: Lizzie Buehler at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Lizzie Buehler —award-winning translator of The Disaster Tourist —for a discussion of her debut novel, The Obsessed , one of Best Life's "Best New Beach Reads Everyone Will Be Talking About This Summer". She will be joined in conversation by Joanna Rakoff —author of the international bestselling memoir My Salinger Year and the award-winning novel A Fortunate Age. About The Obsessed A wildly endearing coming-of-age story and "offbeat tale of obsession" (Caitlin Barasch), following one young woman who reenacts the love plot of her favorite novel only to find herself flailing when she enters a relationship with a fellow literary obsessive. Astrid is obsessed with Russian American novelist Sofiya Sova, whose life trajectory serendipitously parallels Astrid’s own and whose writing seems to encompass every anxious thought Astrid has ever had. Desperate to find the purpose she’s always craved, Astrid begins her PhD program hoping to fully embody the ethos of Sofiya Sova's novel. But when Astrid’s long-term boyfriend, Charlie, breaks up with her after moving to Japan, and a spontaneous Hinge date connects her with a fellow Sofiya Sova obsessive named Elijah, Astrid quickly finds herself transcribing the love plot of her favorite Sofiya Sova novel onto her own life . . . until one day, Elijah begins to pull away and Astrid is left flailing in a life scaffolded by obsession. A bighearted portrait of the anxieties of desire, The Obsessed explores the trials of modern dating, the strange ennui of academia, and the question of how to create a world for yourself within and without the confines of your influences. What we’re left with is a striking portrayal of how a willing reader can bring a text to life, and similarly the animating power of a good novel. Buehler offers intriguing insights into the many ways parasocial relationships t

title: Port Community Pride Day
description: Please join us the Margaret Fuller Neighborhood House on July 11th for Port Community Pride Day, a free event for neighbors, friends, and family in and around Cambridge! Every summer since its inception in 2002, Port Community Pride Day has brought together residents, community organizations, civic leaders, and neighbors from across Cambridge for a free, full-day celebration hosted by the Margaret Fuller Neighborhood House in collaboration with community partners throughout The Port. Reflecting the spirit of the neighborhood it celebrates, the event includes a basketball tournament, community resource fair, live entertainment, free food, and community activities. Community Leadership Awards recognize individuals whose contributions reflect the values that have always defined The Port. This year, we are reinstating an important aspect of Port Community Pride Day: the neighborhood Peace Rally & March. Please join us at 10:00am in Greene-Rose Heritage Park for a short walk that tells a big story--- one of community activism, togetherness, and an over 20-year-long commitment to peace.

title: GRRL HAUS CINEMA : Local Shorts
description: GRRL HAUS: New England Local Showcase The Brattle - July 16 - 8pm GRRL HAUS presents 11 short films by New England filmmakers (or shot in the area), all coming together in one playful, weird, and heartfelt program. This program celebrates the creativity and diversity of local artists and filmmakers in the region. Filmmakers will be in attendance for a Q&A after the screening. The Trip — Ayla Hadimi Ladha, Sarah Feldman Best friends Toby and Lola are having a great night until they must journey across campus to their college's one and only printer. Let's just say it's a trip. Out of Hand — Anne Ciecko Stop motion interactions between shaped ceramics and malleable clay create both a meditative ritual and moments of surprise through shifting perspectives, dimensions, timings, directional movements, and expectations. Pallbearers — Tati Chavitage Pallbearers is an experimental personal documentary that follows the literal and emotional journey of my best friend Phoebe Ferguson and I, as we travel to see her mother’s grave for the first time in her life. Traveling by plane, car, and train from Portland, Oregon to Dublin, Texas, the film follows our ten day journey to reunite mother and daughter. I'd Like To Thank My Wife — Sarah Greenleaf An experimental exploration of the extensive work done by women in the service of their husbands that results in little to no credit. Sticky — Naomi Ash After getting fired from her job, Emi steals a memento from her first love on the night of their final goodbye. The Life of Death — Charlotte Benoit The Grim Reaper learns what it means to be human with the help of a friendly ghost. You Are Not a Memorial — Jaina Cipriano You do not have to burn others names into your skin to be remembered. title: Dance for the Diaspora
description: Dance For The Diaspora (D4D Boston) is a citywide celebration of movement, music, cultural memory, wellness, and collective care featuring workshops, performances, community activations, conversations, DJs, and immersive artistic experiences across Boston and New England. Rooted in Black, Indigenous, diasporic, and LGBTQ+ cultural practices, D4D brings together artists, culture bearers, organizers, and community members to gather, move, learn, and imagine together. Supported by NEFA’s Public Art for Spatial Justice initiative, D4D explores how public art and collective gathering can help create more just, connected, and community-centered public spaces. Developed in partnership with Museum of African American History, Multicultural Arts Center, and The Haus of Glitter, the festival is part of an ongoing residency supporting the development of The Historical Fantasy of Boston. Single Class Passes are available on a sliding scale from $5 to $25, or join us for the entire Saturday experience with a $30 Full Day Pass. 100% of registration proceeds support local artists, culture bearers, and the Museum of African American History’s vital work preserving Black history and stewarding community.

title: Lila Dance Festival
description: 2026 LILA Dance Festival by LILA Productions The sixth annual Lila Dance Festival to take place at Rochester Commons featuring dance, live music, food, vendors and more. Rochester, NH – June 30, 2026 — Lila Dance Festival, New Hampshire’s largest dance festival will take place Saturday, August 29th from 12pm noon to 8pm at Rochester Commons Park with a Sunday, August 30th rain date. Entry is free and attendees are encouraged to bring their own chairs and blankets to enjoy the festival and events throughout the day. Dance performances are a celebration of New Hampshire and greater Northeastern professional companies and choreographers including, Nsquared Dance, Saving Grace Dance Ensemble, Demeo Dance, Annex Contemporary Dance Company, SundanceX, Ballet Arts Collective, and more! The festival will highlight new work by Montreal award winning guest choreographer Andrew Skeels, as well as the premiere of the LiLaB residency works by Trinity Leite and Jacqui Young. Leite’s piece will use rhythm-based movement to explore the emotion of joy. Young’s piece will utilize contemporary movement to explore her time working with correctional facility inmates. The program will feature a diverse range of dance styles, including ballet, contemporary, modern, jazz, tap, hip hop, cultural dance forms, and more, including a performance by returning guest artist Yuval Cohen. For the youngest audience members, Fairytales and Tutus will begin at 2pm, followed by a photo opportunity and meet-and-greet with the characters for children and families. The performance will include visits from Cinderella, Aurora, Belle, and more through an interactive and educational performance aimed to teach young audiences about the structure of classical ballets. Live music by singer/songwriter and Portsmouth Music Hall’s 2025 emerging artists; Skye Darling, and acclaimed New England folk musician Dan Blakeslee. title: Currents of Change: 2nd Annual Kayak Event for ATASK
description: Experience the Charles River from the cockpit of a kayak on this special guided sunset ecotour—now with a renewed sense of purpose. Join the Asian Task Force Against Domestic Violence (ATASK) for our second annual Currents of Change kayaking fundraiser, supporting our mission to empower Asian adults and children who have experienced domestic violence. As you paddle along the river, expert guides will highlight the surrounding wildlife, scenic landscapes, and explore how humans have shaped the environment over time. Whether you're an experienced kayaker or trying it for the first time, all skill levels are welcome. All kayaking equipment is provided, and each guided session is limited to 16 participants to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. While this ecotour is typically offered free to the public, our partners have generously dedicated these tours to benefit ATASK. To participate, we simply ask for a donation of any amount, with all proceeds supporting ATASK's free, multilingual, and culturally responsive services for survivors of domestic violence and their families. Space is limited, and advance registration is strongly encouraged. Date: Thursday, July 16, 2026 Session Times: 4:45 PM 6:30 PM Cost: Donation of any amount to benefit ATASK. Registration: https://secure.qgiv.com/for/ataskpartnershipevents/event/kayak/ Who Can Attend: Open to paddlers of all experience levels. All gear is provided. About ATASK: ATASK provides free, confidential, multilingual, and culturally responsive services to Asian survivors of domestic violence and their families throughout Massachusetts. Every donation helps provide emergency shelter, legal advocacy, housing assistance, and other critical support to help survivors build lives free from abuse.

title: 3rd Annual Cambridge Moth Ball
description: MOTH BALL IS MADE POSSIBLE BY THE CITY, VOLUNTEER-LED ORGANIZATIONS, AND COMMUNITY GROUPS WORKING TOGETHER TO HELP PEOPLE CONNECT WITH THE NATURAL WORLD. Moth Ball is a beautiful summer night under the stars at Fresh Pond’s Kingsley Park. It’s a celebration of night, community, biodiversity, discovery, and, most of all, moths. It’s also a participatory science event where we collect, record, photograph, and identify moths while learning more about their extraordinary lives. Explore the many hands-on activities offered by our partner organizations and get to know moths up close as we share the data and photos we collect with researchers. It’s also part of National Moth Week. This year, we also celebrate the power of moths to inspire the creative imagination of artists. If you’re interested in nature, insects, butterflies, moths, native plants, pollinators, or the amazing wildlife of Cambridge—or if you simply enjoy nighttime, nerding out, and learning something new—this event is for you. We will have special guests, too!

title: Beginner West Coast Swing Lesson & Social Dance to Live Music
description: Come learn west coast swing (WCS)! It's a popular style of partner dancing that's easy to pick up and can be danced to all of your favorite music, and we'll be grooving to two special live acoustic sets by Somerville musician Josh Witt. We'll teach you the basic moves, how to improvise with a partner, and then set you loose to social dance to live music with all of your new friends. The best part? No small talk required. title: BT4W presents The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical
description: Beyond the 4th Wall, in collaboration with the Mayors Summer Youth Employment Program, presents: The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical. The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical is a high- energy adventure based on the bestselling novel by Rick Riordan. When teenager Percy Jackson discovers he's the son of a Greek god, his world is turned upside down. Joined by his friends Annabeth and Grover, Percy embarks on an epic cross-country quest to prevent a war among the gods, uncover the truth about his past, and discover what it really means to be a hero. A talented cast of young performers bringing anthology, music, humor, and adventure to life. Showtimes: Friday, July 31st, 2026 at 7:00PM and Saturday, August 1st, 2026 at 7:00PM The Morse School 40 Granite Street Cambridge MA

title: Tano Jones Revelry Performs At City Winery Boston
description: Rhythm. Life. Melodies. Tales. Harmony. Love. These are the elements that define Tano Jones Revelry, the Detroit-born collective led by singer, songwriter, guitarist, and producer Tano Jones. With a six-string in hand, a dusty hat overhead, and a spirit rooted in connection, Tano Jones creates music for the people and bring it directly to them. Their songs reflect real-life experiences, crafted into poetic narratives that inspire listeners to embrace life fully and dream bigger. Their sound and message speak to anyone searching for hope, unity, and purpose. Known for emotionally driven lyrics and authentic storytelling, the band delivers a powerful live experience that connects deeply with audiences. Friday, August 14, 2026 Doors Open: 6:00PM Show Begins: 7:30PM Tickets are available online at www.TanoJoneRevelry.com/Tour. General Admission: Starting at $30.00* *plus additional fees Haymarket Lounge at City Winery Boston 80 Beverly Street Boston, MA 02114

title: Debbie Lane and the Uncle Sam Band - Free Concert
description: Enjoy a free concert featuring great local musicians every Sunday from 12:30 to 2 pm at the Arlington Visitor Center. This Sunday, Debbie Lane and the Uncle Sam Band play jazz favorites. This free performance is outdoors, weather permitting. See the latest schedule of events and performers in the series at https://ArtsArlington.org/TinyShed. About the Series The Tiny Shed Arts & Discovery Series brings live music, pop-up arts and crafts workshops, art exhibits, and more to the heart of Arlington every weekend from May to October. The series is hosted at the Arlington Visitor Center, located next to Uncle Sam Plaza in Arlington Center, by the Minuteman Bikeway at the intersection of Mass Avenue and Mystic Street. The Visitor Center is open every Saturday and Sunday from May to October. On Sundays from 12:30 pm to 2 pm, the Visitor Center hosts a performance by a local band. Performances are outdoors, weather permitting. Check for weather-related updates on Facebook #artsarlingtonMA or on Instagram @artsarlingtonma. The Tiny Shed series is a collaboration of the Arlington Tourism & Economic Development Committee and ArtsArlington, and is supported by the Mass Cultural Council and Mirak Properties.

title: Somerville Bike Kitchen 11th Birthday Party
description: Join the Somerville Bike Kitchen as we celebrate 11 years of serving the Somerville community! The Somerville Bike Kitchen (SBK) is a volunteer-run bicycle repair cooperative. We provide tools, knowledge, and a workspace for community members to repair their own bicycles and promote cycling as a safe, green, and economical means of transportation and recreation accessible to everyone. Over the past eleven years, thousands of neighbors have walked through our doors to learn new skills, share their knowledge, make new friends, and keep our community rolling. This anniversary is a chance to celebrate everything we've built together! Come enjoy an evening of food, music, and community at the Somerville Armory. Whether you've been a familiar face for years or you're just curious to see what we're all about, we'd love to celebrate with you!

title: Teen Film Screening
description: Join us to celebrate CCTV's Summer Media Institute 2026! Register here! https://bit.ly/SMIScreening2026 Over the course of the summer, participants in CCTV's Summer Media Institute, employed through the Cambridge Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP), spent 6 action-packed weeks with all stages of filmmaking, from concept development, to production, to editing, and beyond! Guided by Teaching Artists and mentors, youth created original short films (horror, documentary, drama, etc.) that reflect their interests, perspectives, and experiences. This final screening marks the culmination of their work and offers an opportunity for family members, friends, community partners, and the public to celebrate these films on the big screen. The evening will feature a selection of student-produced works followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers, dinner and snacks, and raffle prizes!

title: Little Miss and The Boom Presents The Velvet Hour: An Evening of Glamour Music and Cabaret at The Crystal Ball Room
description: Some evenings entertain. The Velvet Hour invites you into another world. Join Little Miss and the Boom at Crystal Ballroom for a two-hour modern vintage cabaret where live music, theatrical storytelling, glamour, and unexpected moments unfold throughout the evening. This is not a traditional concert. It’s an immersive experience designed to transport you from the moment the lights dim until the final encore. The night features Little Miss and the Boom’s signature blend of swing, blues, jazz, and modern vintage favorites, presented in a carefully crafted theatrical production that moves from intimate and sultry to playful, exhilarating, and unforgettable. Adding to the evening, acclaimed burlesque artist Pixie Payne joins the cast for an exclusive performance created especially for The Velvet Hour, seamlessly woven into the night’s story. Whether you’re dressed in vintage glamour or simply looking for an extraordinary night out, you’ll find yourself part of an experience where the audience isn’t just watching the show, they’re inside it. The Evening Includes: • A two-hour live cabaret experience with Little Miss and the Boom • Special guest performance by acclaimed burlesque artist Pixie Payne • Carefully crafted theatrical moments throughout the evening • VIP Velvet Tables available with premium seating, early entry, and a signed copy of Betwixt and Between concert poster • Vintage-inspired attire encouraged. Dress to be seen. One room. One evening. One unforgettable chapter. Welcome to The Velvet Hour.
venue_name: The Crystal Ballroom at Somerville Theater

title: Esh Circus Arts Community Open House
description: Join us for a Community Open House at our Main Studio on Saturday August 22nd from 11am - 2pm! Whether you're curious about circus for yourself or your child, this is a great chance to explore everything our studio has to offer. Try a variety of circus disciplines with our experienced coaches, take a tour of our facilities, meet our staff, and connect with members of our welcoming community. Schedule of activities: 11am - 11:45am - drop in try-it time for Youth ages 4-9 11:15 - 11:35am - Silks & Rope Mini-Taster for Adults (ages 16+) 12pm - 12:45pm - drop in try-it time for Youth ages 10+ 12:15 - 12:35pm - Partner Acro Mini-Taster for Adults (ages 16+) 1pm - 1:20pm - Handstand Mini-Taster for Adults (ages 16+) 1pm - 1:20pm - Aerial Hoop & Trapeze Mini-Taster for Adults (ages 16+) 1:30 - 2pm - Hula Hoop and Juggle Jam for all ages The open house is completely free to attend, but we do need everyone to sign a waiver before participating in activities. The fastest way to do that is to register in advance! We'll also have waivers available to sign on site if needed.

title: Outdoor Movie Night: Wicked
description: Join us in Canal Park at CambridgeSide as we continue our Outdoor Summer Movie Series. Join us for a wickedly good evening starting at 7pm. Kick things off with a "Choose Your Witch” Light-Up Wand Craft followed by a screening of Wicked. It's a summer night the whole family will enjoy. Grab a bite at CanalSide Food + Drink and join us on the lawn. Pre-show entertainment begins at 7pm. Movies begin promptly at 8pm. Plus, enjoy delicious popcorn sponsored by East Cambridge Business Association. Got school supplies? Bring them along! We will be collecting school supplies to benefit the East End House. Suggested donations include new and unused backpacks, pencils & pencil sharpeners, notebooks, binders and more. Link for more details: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/outdoor-movie-night-wicked-tickets-1990656205297?aff=oddtdtcreator&keep_tld=true or CambridgeSide ::: Outdoor Movie Night: Wicked For all movie nights, attendees are encouraged to bring blankets or lawn chairs. Events are free and open to the public. All event elements are first come, first served basis. While supplies last. Please note: all minors must be accompanied by an adult.

title: Pups + Pints
description: Join us on Saturday, August 15, from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM at CanalSide for an afternoon of dogs, drinks, and summer fun! Meet and greet some adorable dogs from Sweet Paws Rescue, browse local pet vendors including Pet Wants Cambridge, The Groom Lagoon, Tandem Vet Care, and A Golden's Rule, and enjoy live music, lawn games, and beverages available for purchase. Free to attend! Bring your pup, grab a drink, and join us for a paw-some afternoon at CanalSide. All well-behaved pups on leashes are welcome. We can't wait to see you there!

title: Foodie Crawl 2026: Eat, Explore, Support local.
description: East Somerville Main Streets invites you to Foodie Crawl 2026, a walking tour through one of Somerville's most flavorful commercial corridors. Sample dishes from Broadway's immigrant-owned restaurants and small businesses, all in one afternoon/evening, while discovering the murals, culture, and community that make East Somerville a destination worth exploring on foot. This event supports the small businesses that make East Somerville what it is: every stop on the crawl is a local, independently-owned restaurant. Come hungry, bring friends, and see Broadway one bite at a time. East Somerville Main Streets is a nonprofit working to support local business, celebrate local culture, and sustain vibrant public space in East Somerville. Learn more at eastsomervillemainstreets.org/foodie-crawl Get your ticket now!

title: Community Art Center: Artist Talk & Book Signing
description: oin Cambridge-raised artists, Sean Alonzo Harris and Dr. Myrah Brown Green in a fireside chat and book signing While Community Art Center’s exhibit: A Place Called Home wraps the walls of Street Theory Collective Gallery, we invite you to join two celebrated Black artists, honoring their Cambridge roots. We will explore what this place called “home” has meant to them, the early influences that nurtured their success, how growing up in Cambridge shaped their creativity, and the role community has played in their lives. This fireside chat will include Sean Alonzo Harris, who attended Community Art Center when he was little, and is now a professional photographer based in Maine. We will also enjoy open discussion and reflections from artist and author, Dr. Myrah Brown Green who has just released her newest book, "Keepers of a Movement: Celebrating the Black Collector". Dr. Green will be available to sign and autograph her stunning art-quality edition book after the chat. Join us for an evening of rich discussion, connection, and inspiration! Lite fare and drink provided.

title: AfterSchool Makerspace & STEM Hub Open House – Kick Off the New School Year!
description: Kick off the new school year with a special hands-on Open House at Guild Hall Learning! Kids ages 8–17 and their families can explore our makerspace, create, build, and compete together. Activities include fast-paced Engineering Challenges, a Build-a-Catapult & Castle Challenge, student creations and showcases, hands-on mini-projects, tools and technology, VR/arcade experiences, and opportunities to meet Guild Hall mentors and other young makers. Come see what makes Guild Hall a unique place to learn, create, and build!

Ave. ) This is part of our Lemonade on the Lawn Series. Light refreshments graciously provided by the Cambridge School of Culinary Arts. All are welcome.

title: CX Summer Nights - Jake Swamp and The Pine & Adam Ezra Group
description: Cambridge Crossing’s CX Summer Nights returns with its final event of the season Thursday, August 20 as part of its free outdoor summer concert series running June through August. The evening will feature live performances by Jake Swamp and The Pine & Adam Ezra Group alongside a rotating lineup of local brews, food trucks, lawn games, and opportunities to support the Cambridge non-profit community. This year’s finale will mark the 10th anniversary of CX Summer Nights.

title: Jen Kearney, Sam Newcomer, Sam Bayer at McCarthy's Sunday Sept 13
description: Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents singer/songwriters Jen Kearney, Sam Newcomer and Sam Bayer on Sunday afternoon September 13. The show begins at 4:00 pm and admission is $15 in advance, $20 at the door. McCarthy's is at 1920 Mass. Ave, Cambridge, across from the Porter Square Red Line T station. For advance tickets visit https://tickets.24hourmusic.com/eventperformances.asp?evt=1866. For more information call McCarthy's at 617-945-1887, visit https://www.mccarthystoad.com or https://www.facebook.com/SomervilleSongwriterSessions or email SomervilleSongwriterSessions@gmail.com. Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents contemporary folk singer/songwriters in concert on the second Sunday afternoon of each month. Each performer will do a solo set, followed by a round-robin with all three performers. McCarthy's features live music in a comfortable, listening room setting, and features a full menu and bar. Our 9/13 performers: Originally from Boston, Jen Kearney has spent some time seasoning her particular style of original music. Her sound is an amalgamation of Soul, R&B, Funk, Rock, and Latin. Kearney’s music and attention to lyrics have met critical acclaim nationally and internationally. Her latest album Gas Station Poet was listed as one of WBUR's favorite albums of 2025. She is a two-time New England Music Award nominee for soul/r&b act of the year, and has shared the stage with such luminaries as Maceo Parker, Los Lobos, Daryl Hall and Mavis Staples. "Jen Kearney is a gifted singer who can belt out a song with the best of them. She puts a refreshing new spin on funk music with thoughtfully conceived lyrics… simply mesmerizing." -Steve Morse (Billboard/Rolling Stone). More on Jen at https://jenkearney.com. Sam Newcomer is a singer-songwriter and children's musician based in Roslindale. He writes observational, heartfelt songs that dig into the everyday, pulling from influences like Carole King, Bill Withers, Josh Ritter, and Kasey
cost: $15 in advance (discount with code SSS), $20 day of show

title: Midday Music: Grooversity
description: Acclaimed percussionist and educator Marcus Santos leads the Grooversity ensemble of drummers in an engaging journey through the musical traditions of his native Bahia, Brazil’s first capital. The performance blends Afro-Brazilian rhythms, the powerful energy of carnival percussion, and contemporary Baile Funk, creating an experience that is both culturally rich and highly interactive.

title: Outdoor Movie: Encanto
description: Join us for a summer screening of Encanto (PG). This film is presented in collaboration with MIT Graduate Residential Life, and is first come, first served regardless of registration. Seating is limited - we recommend bringing a blanket or a chair. All minors must be accompanied by a responsible adult. Responsible adults, please keep a close eye on your kids.

title: Midday Music & Free Bike Tune Ups!
description: Enjoy live hip-hop and R&B music curated by The Cambridge Hip-Hop Collective and free safety checks with a bicycle technician from Casa Bikes. Safety checks will take place on a first come, first served basis, regardless of advance registration. This is a popular event - we recommend arriving early to get a spot in line!

Student volunteers will be on-site to help you register to vote or update your voter registration. title: Community Service Fund Book Sale
description: Bookworms, this is your moment! Stop by the MIT Community Service Fund Used Book Sale to discover a large selection of unbelievably priced textbooks, nonfiction, novels, and more.

title: Midday Music with Joseph Ntaimo
description: Enjoy music by Joseph Ntaimo, an MIT graduate student studying mechanical engineering with a focus in musical robotics. Alongside an upbeat DJ set, Ntaimo will play a ferro-instrument (a hyperinstrument that makes ferrofluid respond to music by altering the magnetic field) and other experimental musical devices he’s developing.

title: Fall Party
description: Join us to celebrate the season with live music from Jazz World Trio, hands-on art activities, free popcorn and cotton candy, face painting, and more!

title: Screening of Presence
description: Join us for a midday screening exploring how public life has been staged, recorded, and remembered on screen. Presence is a film installation by Jingrong Zhang, supported by the Council for the Arts at MIT (CAMIT). Drawing on archival and cinematic footage across cultures and historical periods, the work assembles a "global supercut" of public gatherings: moments of solitude, chance encounters, street life, and collective assembly. As the montage builds from isolated figures to dense crowds, it invites viewers to consider how strangers come together in public space, and how those moments of shared presence have been captured on screen across a century of image-making. Every crowd on screen was once as present as we are now.

title: Midday Music & Soup: Joseph Borsellino and Friends
description: Join saxophonist/composer Joseph Borsellino III and bassist Tony Irons for Mkeka, their captivating new project featuring effects-laden textures and intricate grooves drawn from African diasporic music. While you listen, enjoy a delicious hot cup of soup from Souper Roll Up Cafe (on us, while supplies last!). To keep things sustainable, we encourage you to bring your own mug or bowl. If you do, you’ll get a special sweet treat!

title: Stitch and Screen
description: Join us for a cozy screening of A League of Their Own (PG), presented in collaboration with the PKG Center for Social Impact and the MIT Women’s League. Bring your craft projects along and feel free to sew or stitch while you watch; we’ll keep the lights up!

title: Crafternoon with Alie Reilinger
description: Join artist Alie Reilinger, printer at Cambridge-based Albertine Press and owner of Yellow Leg Studios, for an afternoon of printmaking. Please note that capacity is limited; space is available on a first come, first served basis regardless of registration.

title: Birds of Prey at Mount Auburn Cemetery
description: Join licensed raptor rehabilitators Julie Anne Collier and Jim Parks as they lead a live educational program on Raptors of the Northeast. Julie and Jim of WINGMASTERS will introduce attendees to live birds of prey native to New England. This presentation will explain predation, the birds’ place at the top of the food web, their different hunting adaptations and their status in a rapidly changing world. Two sessions are being offered on Sunday, August 23 at 10:30am and1:00pm. Space is limited, Registration required. PLEASE NOTE: By request of program facilitators, this event is for ages 6 and up only. All attendees must be at least 6 years old to attend.

title: Groundwork Somerville's Harvest Festival
description: On Saturday, October 3 from 12-4pm, Groundwork Somerville invites you to join us as we bring our neighbors together for our annual Harvest Festival! South Street will transform into a vibrant celebration of the growing season and the incredible community that makes Somerville thrive. Participate in free workshops like natural dyeing, fermentation, or making an herbal balm – all using plants grown right here on our community farm! You can also join a community art project that will live on the farm, meet the local organizations and artists tabling, and enjoy live music from the incredible musicians, Jade Faria and Los Mambiseros - get ready to dance!

title: Iveria: Traditional Georgian folk music
description: Join us for our Lemonade on the Lawn Series, this week with Iveria, a wonderful chorus performing traditional Georgian (the country, not the state) folk music. Refreshments provided by Cambridge School of Culinary Arts. Note: this is a revised date

title: Idle Fest 3.0 - Made in One Week
description: IDLE FEST 3: ONE WEEK OF DEVISING. 12 ARTISTS. ONE NIGHT ONLY. What happens when performing artists from completely different worlds meet, collaborate, and have less than one week to create something together? That’s Idle Fest. We bring together performers of all kinds- actors, dancers, musicians, comedians, drag artists, puppeteers, and more to form unexpected creative teams. Most artists meet for the first time through this process, then have just one week to dream up, rehearse, and create an original performance. The result? A night of brand-new, one-of-a-kind performances that push artists outside their comfort zones. 🎭 You won’t know exactly what you’re going to see. Neither will we. Join us August 29th for a night of wild collaborations, exciting combinations, and performances you’ll only see once. PWYW snacks and soda will be available. Subscribe to our Patreon for exclusive behind-the-scenes content: https://www.patreon.com/cw/IdleHandsTheatreCollective Want a taste of the chaos? Watch the first two Idle Fests for free on YouTube: Idle Hands Collective on YouTube 🎟️ Limited Pay What You Can tickets are now available for presale.

title: The Honey Steelers Free Concert
description: Music for all ages! Sweet grooves, soulful delivery, and a late-summer evening on the Charles. The Honey Steelers bring their signature sound to Riverstage at Herter Park for a free outdoor show that's equal parts laid-back and unforgettable.

title: Of Earth and Sky
description: "Juventas’s Neighborhood Series features our same phenomenal musicians in informal free concerts — right in your neighborhood. Soak in the last few glimmers of summer with this collection of pieces inspired by natural landscapes and changing seasons. Featuring works by Rachel Panitch, Carson Cooman, Evan Fein, Alasdair Fraser, and Natalie Haas. With performances by Hannah O'Brien and Matthew Smith."
venue_name: Longfellow-House Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site

title: All We Are
description: Spanning generations and continents, the composers on this program ask what it means to endure, to hold multiple identities, and to cherish what is most fragile and fleeting. All We Are honors moments, both ordinary and remarkable, whose significance is often only understood in hindsight. Featuring works by Kian Ravaei, Reena Esmail, and David Biedenbender, and a world premiere by Oliver Caplan. With performances by Julia Scott Carey, Celine Ferro, Nicholas Johnson, and Kelley Hollis.

title: Thomas Schmidt: Center Stage
description: This special solo concert, curated by the artist himself, showcases a mesmerizing array of percussion instruments. It centers on the complex beauty of the natural world and the pioneering scientists who have explored its wonders, from microscopic particles to voyages through outer space. It also highlights Thomas Schmidt’s exceptional musicianship and artistry, offering audiences an intimate glimpse into his unique musical voice. Featuring works by Stephanie Ann Boyd, Cole Reyes, Salina Fisher, Evan Williams, Victoria Bond, and a world premiere by Oliver Caplan. With Performances by Thomas Schmidt, Julia Scott Carey, and Ryan Shannon.

title: Crossings
description: A nation of immigrants, the strength of America has always been rooted in its many diverse voices. Crossings celebrates the ancestry, community, and tenacity that defines this rich culture. Featuring works by Oliver Caplan, Brian Shankar Adler, Clarice Assad, Ursula Kwong-Brown, and a world premiere by Steven Sérpa. With performances by Nicholas Southwick, Celine Ferro, Ryan Shannon, Lu Yu, Julia Scott Carey, Thomas Schmidt, and Kelley Hollis.

title: Peter Liu Headlines the Comedy Studio
description: The hilarious Peter Liu will be headlining the Comedy Studio in Harvard Square this Wednesday (9/2)! Now based in New York City, Peter is back in town for one night only at one of Greater Boston’s very best comedy rooms. Raised in China, Australia, New Zealand, and the exotic land of New Jersey, Peter brings an outsider’s eye and an insider’s charm to the stage. He has opened for Ronny Chieng and Judah Friedlander and performed at some of the biggest venues and festivals in comedy, including The Wilbur, The Laugh Factory, The Comedy Store, The San Francisco Comedy Festival, and the New York Comedy Festival. If you like your comedy smart, personal, and a little unhinged — don’t miss Peter! He’ll be joined by Boston comedian Jason Fishman and NYC’s Peng Dang. It’s going to be a blast. We hope to see you there!
street_address: 5 John F. Kennedy St, Cambridge, MA, 02138
